## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want each provider entry in a model's `providers`
list to declare the priorities it may serve (`priorities: [low, medium]`), and
to **delete `priority_routes` entirely**, so that priority routing is declared
once, in one place, in the provider definition I am already editing — instead
of maintaining a second, name-referencing index that duplicates the chain and
is easy to drift or get wrong.

## Problem statement

Priority routing is currently declared twice for every model in
`proxy/config.yaml`:

1. `models.<name>.providers` — the ordered provider definitions; and
2. `models.<name>.priority_routes` — a map from priority to an ordered list of
   provider **names**, resolved back against (1) at request time by
   `proxy/proxy/priority.py::_resolve_chain_entries`.

This gives two competing sources of truth for the same chain, and the operator
has to keep them synchronised by hand. Concrete mess re-verified against the
tree on 2026-10-24:

- `plan`, `author` and `code` carry **byte-identical** 7-entry `providers`
  lists (`plan == author == code` compares `True`), each with the **identical**
  5-name `low` list — 21 provider definitions and 15 repeated names. Verified
  provider order: `local-qwen3`, `munitoai-free`, `opencode-go-3`,
  `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`, `munitoai`, `deepseek-flash`.
- Membership in a priority chain is invisible from the provider definition: to
  answer "is `munitoai` used for low work?" you must read a different block.
- Name references add a failure mode with no upside: an unresolvable name is
  logged as `priority_routes: unknown provider name %r … skipping entry` and
  routing silently continues with a shorter chain.
- A new provider inherits priority membership only if someone remembers to add
  its name to the right list(s) — and forgetting means it is silently absent
  from (or, for a paid tier, silently present in) a `low` chain.
- Ordering is likewise stated twice: `providers` order *and* each
  `priority_routes` list order, which must agree.
- Nothing validates `priority_routes` at load: `_validate_config`
  (`proxy/proxy/utils.py:650`) validates prompts, chain-hold and compaction,
  but nothing provider- or priority-shaped.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Delete `priority_routes`.** No compatibility shim, no override path, no
  "both work" period: the two-representations problem is the whole complaint.
- **Priority membership lives only on provider definitions**, as a
  `priorities` key whose value is a **list** of valid priorities
  (`[low, medium, high]`, `[medium, high]`, …).
- **No implication between tiers.** A provider labelled `medium` is *not*
  thereby eligible for `low`; membership is exactly the list written. (An
  earlier idea — a scalar threshold where `medium` implied `low` — was rejected
  because it would have put the paid `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` tiers into
  the `low` chain, breaking AC6 of LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX.)
- **Per-model divergence is a requirement, not an accident.** The label sits on
  each model's own inline provider entry, so *plan* may later add an expensive
  model while *code* keeps the current set and *author* gains a
  less code-oriented one, without touching the other models.

## Design

Resolution becomes a filter over the model's own provider list, in list order
(no name lookup, no rank table, no monotonicity assumption):

```python
chain(P) = [p for p in providers if P in p["priorities"]]   # order = providers order
```

- Model-level opt-in, fail-closed: if **any** provider in a model declares
  `priorities`, **every** provider in that model must declare it (otherwise the
  chain would depend on an implicit default, which is exactly the silent-leak
  bug class this item removes). A model that declares no `priorities` anywhere
  keeps today's behaviour: every provider eligible for every priority (this is
  what `embed`, `github` and `private` do today — they have no
  `priority_routes`). That legacy full-list default is therefore scoped to
  *unlabelled* models only.
- **No implicit fallback for a labelled model.** Today
  `priority.py::effective_chain_for_request` re-adds the full `providers` list
  when the chain it obtained is empty (`if not chain: chain = providers`). For a
  labelled model an empty filtered chain must **not** be widened that way —
  that is the same silent leak in another disguise. See Q6 for the open
  question on what a labelled model with no provider for a priority should do
  (load-time rejection vs. request-time exhaustion).
- A model that still contains `priority_routes` must fail at load with a
  migration message (fail-closed; a stale overlay must not silently lose its
  routing).
- Validation (load-time `ValueError`): non-list value, empty list, unknown
  priority name, duplicate entry, and the partially-labelled-model rule above.

Behaviour-equivalent target for the shipped config (this is the refactor, not a
routing change):

| Model | `low` | `medium` / `high` |
|---|---|---|
| `plan`, `author`, `code` | `local-qwen3`, `munitoai-free`, `opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go` | full 7-entry `providers` list |
| `compact` | `opencode-go-compact`, `deepseek-flash-compact` | full 2-entry `providers` list |
| `embed`, `github`, `private` | full `providers` list | full `providers` list |

⇒ labels: `local-qwen3`, `munitoai-free`, `opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`,
`opencode-go`, `opencode-go-compact`, `deepseek-flash-compact` =
`[low, medium, high]`; `munitoai`, `deepseek-flash` = `[medium, high]`.
`local-embed`, `github-primary`, `local-qwen3` (private) need no labels.

## Scope

In scope:

- `proxy/config.yaml`: add `priorities` to every provider entry of the
  priority-routed models; delete the four `priority_routes` blocks and their
  now-stale rationale comments —
  `plan` line 569, `author` line 731, `code` line 900, `compact` line 950
  (whose comment "Declared explicitly to satisfy the per-model
  `priority_routes` schema (AC2)" at 946-949 also goes); move/retain the
  rationale in the provider definitions and the docs.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`: delete `_resolve_chain_entries` (342); replace
  `provider_chain_for_priority` (379) with the filter; drop the empty-chain
  full-list fallback for labelled models in `effective_chain_for_request`
  (447, fallback at 460-462); update the module docstring (32-41),
  `priority_routing_profile` (274) and `apply_local_preference`-adjacent
  docstrings that currently document `priority_routes` as the mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py`: add the provider `priorities` /
  removed-`priority_routes` validation and wire it into `_validate_config`
  (650), following the existing delegate pattern (`_validate_chain_hold_config`
  660, `_validate_compaction_config` 674, `_validate_prompt_configs` 689) —
  i.e. a `validate_priority_config(cfg) -> list[str]` in `provider.py`
  validated from `utils.py`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: **comment-only** edits — the two call-site
  comments name `priority_routes` (`8186-8188`, `8827-8829`). The functional
  integration is `effective_chain_for_request` (imported at line 48, called at
  8196 and 8837) and needs no change beyond the above.
- Docs: `proxy/README.md` (line 18 bullet; 1188-1193 "Each model may declare
  `priority_routes` (AC2)" paragraph), `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the off-peak
  section at 225-260, which writes the `low` chain as `low: [...]` and must
  describe the labels instead), provider field table in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
  (97-108 — the `| Field | Type | Required | Description |` table where
  `priorities` belongs, next to `max_context_tokens`). `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`
  does **not** exist yet (LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY is at `plan_complete`), so it is
  cross-referenced rather than edited.
- Tests:
  - `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py`: rewrite `TestProviderChains`
    (164-200, currently asserts name resolution / unknown-name skip) and
    `TestModeRemoval::test_models_declare_priority_routes` (382-389, asserts the
    live config has `priority_routes.low`) — AC1 forbids the string anywhere.
  - `proxy/tests/test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py`: the `_target_chain_entries`
    shim (131-141, synthesises `priority_routes`) and
    `TestLiveConfigInvariants::test_fully_paid_tiers_never_enter_a_low_chain`
    (194-204, reads `routes = model.get("priority_routes")`); the remaining
    `TestTargetChainShape` (153), `TestWindowGating` (228), `TestFailoverScope`
    (281) and `TestRoutingProfileDocs` (331) assertions keep their intent while
    the chains are derived from labels.
  - `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`: whole-entry equality against
    literals — `providers[1] == MUNITOAI_FREE_ENTRY` (89, 129) and
    `providers[paid_index] == MUNITOAI_ENTRY` (110, 133). The fixtures must gain
    the new `priorities` key (or the assertions become key-subset checks) or
    they break on the re-labelled config.

Out of scope:

- Any routing behaviour change: no chain membership, order, window, budget or
  failover semantics change. `available_times` line count must be unchanged
  (136 matching lines across `proxy/tests/*.py` today; the config lines
  themselves are byte-frozen by AC4).
- Per-priority *ordering* (e.g. `munitoai` first for `high` only). It was
  expressible only via `priority_routes`, and is deliberately dropped; it is
  not used by any model today. Record it as a known limitation, not a gap.
- DRYing the duplicated per-model provider definitions into YAML anchors or a
  shared provider library (see the anchor caveat in Q5).

## Constraints

- **Behaviour-neutral by construction.** No chain membership, order, window,
  budget or failover change; AC3 (frozen equivalence) and AC8 (unchanged
  off-peak intent) are the gate, and AC4 forbids any non-`priorities` config
  diff.
- **One mechanism, no compatibility window.** `priority_routes` is deleted
  outright (no shim, no override, no deprecation phase); a stale config that
  still declares it must fail loudly at load with a migration message.
- **No tier implication.** A label lists exactly the priorities a provider may
  serve; `medium` never implies `low`.
- **Per-model labels are independent.** No shared/global membership table, and
  no change may introduce cross-model coupling.
- **Repository boundaries.** Implementation touches only `proxy/`; agent
  infrastructure (`.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`) is out of bounds and issues
  there are reported, not edited.
- **Tests run through the test skill** (`/skill:test`), never ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes` is gone as a *mechanism*: it appears in no live config
   (`proxy/config.yaml`) and in no routing code path (no runtime read, no name
   resolution, no route map). The only permitted occurrences are the three the
   removal itself mandates: the load-time deprecation guard in
   `validate_priority_config` and its migration message (AC5), that guard's
   tests (AC5), and the migration documentation (AC9).
   Baseline before the change (`git grep -c`, 27 matching lines in 6 files):
   `config.yaml` 5 (569/731/900/949/950), `priority.py` 7, `provider.py` 2
   (8187/8828), `README.md` 3, `test_priority_routing.py` 8,
   `test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py` 2.
   **Amended 2026-10-24 (producer-accepted, LP-C0MVMKBH4O002JC4N):** the
   original wording required `git grep -n priority_routes` to return nothing at
   all, which is unsatisfiable together with AC5 (a test must declare the key to
   prove it is rejected) and AC9 (the docs must state the removal and how to
   migrate). The producer accepted the mechanism-level form above. After the
   change `git grep -n priority_routes` = 22 lines in 6 files — 3 in the guard,
   7 in the guard's tests, 12 in the migration docs — and **zero** in
   `config.yaml` or any routing path.
2. Every provider entry of `plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` declares a
   `priorities` list; `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` declare exactly
   `[medium, high]` and appear in no `low` chain; all other entries declare
   `[low, medium, high]`.
3. An equivalence test derives every chain from the `priorities` labels and
   asserts byte-identical equality with the pre-change chains, frozen as
   literals in the test: `low` = the 5-entry list for plan/author/code and the
   2-entry list for `compact`; `medium`/`high` = the full `providers` list for
   every model; `embed`, `github`, `private` = full list for all three
   priorities.
4. `git diff` for `proxy/config.yaml` shows **zero** changed `available_times`
   lines, and every provider entry's non-`priorities` keys are byte-identical
   to before.
5. Load-time validation rejects, each with a test: a non-list `priorities`
   value; an empty list; an unknown priority name; a duplicate entry; a model
   where some but not all providers declare `priorities`; and a model that
   still declares `priority_routes` (clear migration message naming the
   replacement key).
6. `provider_chain_for_priority` contains no name lookup and no provider-name
   warning path (`_resolve_chain_entries` is deleted); chain order is the
   model's `providers` order, proved by a test using an out-of-alphabetical
   order.
7. Per-model divergence is proved by a test: two models with identical provider
   lists except for one provider's `priorities` value resolve to different
   chains, with no cross-model coupling.
8. Priors preserved: `proxy/tests/test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py` passes
   unchanged in intent — in-window eligibility, out-of-window skip-and-fall-
   through, per-key-429 sibling failover, same-domain-5xx exclusion — now
   expressed through `priorities` labels.
9. Docs: `README.md`, `docs/routing.md`, `MODEL_ADD.md` and the `priority.py`
   docstrings describe `priorities` as the one mechanism, state that
   `priority_routes` is removed and how to migrate, and record that
   per-priority ordering is not supported.
10. Full suite green via `/skill:test`; the change is behaviour-neutral
    (no routing, window, budget or failover change is claimed or observed).
11. A labelled model never silently widens a filtered chain: an empty
    `chain(P)` is either a load-time error or an explicit request-time
    exhaustion, never a fallback to the full `providers` list — with a test for
    the chosen rule (see Q6, pending producer confirmation).

## Key Files (predicted; line numbers verified 2026-10-24)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `embed` 338, `github` 346, `private` 357 (unlabelled,
  unchanged); `plan` 383 (providers 388-568, `priority_routes` 569, stale
  rationale comment 550-568); `author` 584 (`priority_routes` 731); `code` 753
  (`priority_routes` 900); `compact` 922 (providers 923-948, `priority_routes`
  950 with its 946-949 AC2 comment).
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — module docstring 32-41,
  `priority_routing_profile` 274, `_resolve_chain_entries` 342 (delete),
  `provider_chain_for_priority` 379, `effective_chain_for_request` 447 with the
  empty-chain fallback at 460-462.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` — `_validate_config` 650 and its delegate pattern
  (660 / 674 / 689).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — comment-only 8186-8188, 8827-8829; import 48 and
  calls 8196 / 8837 unchanged.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — `TestProviderChains` 164-200,
  `TestModeRemoval::test_models_declare_priority_routes` 382-389.
- `proxy/tests/test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py` — `_target_chain_entries`
  131-141, `TestTargetChainShape` 153, `TestLiveConfigInvariants` 170
  (priority_routes read at 199), `TestWindowGating` 228, `TestFailoverScope`
  281, `TestRoutingProfileDocs` 331.
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` — entry literals 29-70 and the
  equality assertions at 89, 110, 129, 133.
- `proxy/README.md` 18 and 1188-1193; `proxy/docs/routing.md` 225-260;
  `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` 97-108.

## Effort and risk

- **Effort: S** — net code deletion (a ~30-line name resolver replaced by a
  filter), config re-labelling, validation (~20 lines), docs, tests.
- **Risk: Low** — behaviour-neutral by construction and proved by the frozen
  equivalence test (AC3) plus the unchanged off-peak tests (AC8). The two real
  hazards are (a) a silent default for an unlabelled provider in a labelled
  model, removed by AC5's fail-closed validation, and (b) the empty-filtered-
  chain widening at `effective_chain_for_request` 460-462, removed by AC11.
  Secondary hazard: whole-entry test literals
  (`test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`) fail the moment the config gains
  `priorities` — a mechanical fix, but a build-red window if forgotten.
- **Scope-creep risk: moderate.** The refactor makes the duplicated per-model
  provider blocks painful to read (21 near-identical definitions), which will
  tempt a YAML-anchor/shared-library dedup in the same change. Do not: Q5 shows
  an anchor shares `priorities` and would silently destroy per-model routing.
  Record any such idea as a new linked work item instead.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX** — Enable low-priority fallback to opencode-go during
  its off-peak windows (**completed**; source of this item). Its AC6 (paid tiers
  never in a `low` chain) and AC8 (live-window verification via child
  LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO, also **completed**) constrain this refactor: the derived
  chains must be identical to the ones that item shipped.
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** — Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode
  (completed): introduced `priority_routes` (its AC2 allowed "an equivalent
  per-provider eligibility field"); this item adopts that alternative and
  removes the list form.
- **LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY** — Consolidate and document the provider
  fallback-chain configuration model (open, `plan_complete`): the new
  `priorities` field belongs in that reference document; sequence so the two do
  not contradict.
- **LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P** — Quota-aware OpenCode Go surge (completed): touched
  the same window-eligibility predicate; confirms `available_times` stays a
  dynamic gate, independent of this static membership label.
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** — Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating
  (completed): owns the window-gating assertions that AC8 must keep passing.
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** — Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak)
  (completed): the config edit that produced the current 5-entry `low` chains.
- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — Stale `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` fixtures
  (open, low): same "config schema moved on, fixtures did not" failure pattern;
  not a blocker.

## Sequencing

No hard blocker. LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO (live-window verification) and
LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX (the parent fallback work) are both **completed**, so the
conditional "either order is safe" no longer applies: this item can run now.
If LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY (provider fallback-chain reference doc) starts first,
land the `priorities` wording there and reference it from here to avoid
contradictory documentation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** – Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating (completed)
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** – Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) (completed)
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** – Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode (X-Priority header + per-model priority tiers) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- No relevant repository file matches: the automated scan's three hits are the
  unrelated `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts*.txt` prompt
  corpora (matched on generic tokens such as `absent`/`ac2`).

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search "priority_routes" --json` (12 hits) plus a keyword sweep of the
`priorities` / provider-chain vocabulary found **no item satisfying this item's
ACs**: LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA *introduced* `priority_routes` and is closed;
LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX / LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I only edited chain *membership*; and
LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY documents the fallback-chain model without removing
`priority_routes`. No overlap, no rewrite needed.

## Appendix: design questions & decisions

### Q1. Scalar threshold (`priority: medium` ⇒ also `low`) or explicit list?
**Decision: explicit list.** Rejected the threshold: (a) the operator's stated
implication direction (`medium` implies `low`) would have admitted the paid
`munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` tiers to the `low` chain, breaking
LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX AC6; (b) the workable direction (`low` implies medium/high)
is only a compression of the general case and would re-introduce a hidden
implication between tiers, which the operator explicitly does not want; (c) a
monotone interval cannot express "medium + high but not low" plus a future
"low only" entry in the same model.

### Q2. Key name?
**`priorities`** — a list-valued key; `priority` (singular) reads like
a scalar and was ambiguous about implication direction. Document it in the
`MODEL_ADD.md` provider field table.

### Q3. What about a model that declares no `priorities` at all?
Full `providers` list for every priority — today's behaviour for `embed`,
`github`, `private`. But a *partially* labelled model is a load-time error
(model-level opt-in), so adding a provider never silently joins or leaves a
chain.

### Q4. Keep a `priority_routes` escape hatch for per-priority ordering?
**No.** The operator's reason for this item is that two representations are
confusing. Per-priority ordering is unused today; record it as unsupported and
revisit only if a real need appears.

### Q5. Caveat if someone later DRYs the duplicated provider dicts
A YAML anchor (or a shared provider library) shares the whole dict including
`priorities`, so per-model labels require either un-anchoring or
a per-model `priorities` override merged over the anchor. Recorded so a future
dedup does not silently destroy per-model routing.

### Q6. OPEN QUESTION — what does an *empty* `chain(P)` mean for a labelled model?
Discovered during intake review (2026-10-24): today
`effective_chain_for_request` (`priority.py:460-462`) re-adds the full
`providers` list whenever the selected chain is empty. For an unlabelled model
that is the documented backward-compatible default; for a labelled model whose
providers all omit `P` it is a silent widening to the paid tiers — the same
bug class this item removes. It is not exercised by the shipped config (every
model labels a provider for every priority), so AC3/AC4 are unaffected.

Options:

- **(a) Load-time rejection + no runtime widening (recommended).** Validation
  requires ≥1 provider per priority for a labelled model, and
  `effective_chain_for_request` returns the filtered chain as-is for labelled
  models. Rationale: the cheap window (`server.priority_window`, local
  01:00-10:00) caps *every* request to `low`, so a model with no `low`-eligible
  provider would be unusable for nine hours a day — failing at startup is far
  better than a 503 storm at 02:00.
- **(b) Allow empty chains, no widening.** Return `[]`; the existing exhaustion
  path reports it as a request-time 503. Allows a deliberately restrictive
  model, at the cost of a runtime failure mode that only appears inside the
  cheap window.
- **(c) Keep the full-list fallback for empty chains.** Preserves today's
  code path exactly, but re-introduces the silent paid-tier leak this item
  exists to remove — contradicts Q3's fail-closed rule.

**Recommended:** (a) — fail closed at load, and never widen a labelled model's
chain at request time.
**Status: RESOLVED — option (a) implemented** (AC11, commit a0093621). The
validator requires at least one provider per priority for a labelled model, and
`effective_chain_for_request` / `provider_chain_for_priority` never widen a
labelled model's filtered chain. (b) and (c) were rejected: (b) defers the
failure into the cheap window, and (c) re-introduces the paid-tier leak.

### Q7. Scope corrections found while verifying the tree
Not operator questions, recorded for traceability: (i) `provider.py` carries two
`priority_routes` *comments* (8186-8188, 8827-8829) which AC1's repo-wide grep
also covers, though the original brief listed provider.py as "no change
expected"; (ii) `test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` asserts whole-entry equality
against literals and therefore breaks when `priorities` is added; (iii)
`test_priority_routing.py::TestModeRemoval::test_models_declare_priority_routes`
(382-389) was missing from the test scope. All three are now in Scope and Key
Files.

# Correlated measurement: does `lease_state` / `prefill_eta_seconds` match reality? Follow-up to `discovered-from:LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` (Publish truthful local capacity on `/llama/local/status`). The status-payload work is delivered separately; this item verifies that the new signals actually predict what they claim to. ## Goal (user story) As an operator, I want a measured before/after comparison of dispatch denials against real local work, so I know whether gating on `lease_state` and `prefill_eta_seconds` removes the idle-lease false-busy dispatch failures rather than just changing the shape of the payload. ## Baseline (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23) - `local_dispatch_denied` **2,641** (2,633 with `active=2` lease records) while local decoded only **29.3%** of wall clock. - Worst hour (04:00–05:00): **187** denials at **2.5%** local busy. ## What to measure (same 24h window length, after the fields are live) 1. Denials per hour, and the share attributable to `idle_leased` slots versus genuine `prefill_bound` / `saturated` conditions. 2. Local busy fraction (decode wall-clock share) versus the denials, to confirm the pool was genuinely idle when denials happened. 3. Accuracy of `prefill_eta_seconds`: predicted versus observed prefill duration for dispatches that ran (p50/p90 error). ### Where each measurement comes from (verified 2026-10-22 against the live payload and `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`) - **M1 — denial attribution.** `local_dispatch_denied` lines carry only `session=`, `owner=`, `active=`, `cold_start=` — **no `lease_state`**. The attributable signal sits on the adjacent `local_admission_guard` line (`decision=reject|admit reason= busy_slots=N in_flight_prefills=N free_slot= priority=

`), so attribute each denial by joining its timestamp block to that guard record. The `idle_leased` vs `prefill_bound`/`saturated` split is then derived from guard reason + `busy_slots`/`free_slot` corroborated by M2's busy fraction. - **M2 — local busy fraction.** Already emitted by the deterministic CLI (`dispatch_denied` counts plus `BusyStats.busy_pct`); no extension needed. - **M3 — prefill ETA accuracy.** Predicted: `prefill_eta_seconds` on `status_request` lines (4,325 such lines in the current log; `status_schema_version=2`). Observed: llama-server `prompt eval time = ms / tokens` lines, already parsed by `llama_log_parser.py` as `prompt_eval` samples. The p50/p90 prediction error itself is **not** computed today. ### Required CLI extension (in scope for this item) `analyze_proxy_usage.py` counts denials and busy time but neither aggregates denials by guard reason nor computes prefill-ETA prediction error. Because the item's method requirement is the deterministic CLI, extend it rather than writing ad-hoc greps: - per-hour denial counts split by `local_admission_guard` reason + `busy_slots` / `free_slot` (M1); - prefill ETA predicted-vs-observed error, p50/p90, for dispatches that ran (M3). Write unit tests for both aggregations **before** the implementation (test-first). ## Acceptance Criteria - A report exists under `/home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/` covering a 24 h window after the payload change is live, and it presents all three measurements above (M1 per-hour denial attribution by guard reason, M2 local busy fraction versus denials, M3 prefill-ETA predicted-versus-observed error at p50/p90). - Denials-per-hour and local-busy are compared against the stated baseline, with an explicit verdict: signal matches reality / does not / inconclusive. - Any mismatch is filed as a new work item with the supporting log evidence. ## Risks / notes - Dependency `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` is **completed** and the payload is live (`status_schema_version: 2`; per-slot `lease_state` / `phase` / `prefill_eta_seconds` and top-level `capacity_hint` present), so this item is no longer blocked. - The baseline window (2,641 denials at 29.3% busy) predates the payload change, so the post-change window must be selected explicitly (`--start`/`--end`) rather than the CLI's default last-24h window. - Use the deterministic analysis CLI (`/skill:proxy-usage-analysis`) rather than ad-hoc log greps, so numbers are reproducible.

# Harden proxy start against foreground invocation being killed by tool-call timeouts

## Problem statement

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` ends with `exec "$PY_BIN" -m uvicorn proxy.server:app …`, so the
server runs inside whatever process group launched the script. When an agent runs the script in the
foreground under a bash tool call, the harness's tool timeout (60 s) SIGKILLs the whole process
group, killing uvicorn mid-startup with no `Shutting down` line — and because the same invocation
passed `--restart` (which had already SIGTERM'd the previous instance), the proxy is left
completely offline with no error surfacing anywhere except the tool result.

Observed once on 2026-10-20 (session `herdr-1792503008-530778-31323`, tool result
`Command timed out after 60 seconds`). llama-server (preserved by the restart gate) and TTS
(spawned via `nohup` inside the proxy) survived; only the foreground uvicorn died.

## Users and user stories

- **Agent session running a start/restart** — "As an agent asked to restart the proxy, I want the
  server to keep running after my tool call ends or times out, so that a restart never leaves the
  service dead."
- **Operator debugging the proxy** — "As an operator, I sometimes want to watch the server in the
  foreground; I want that to be an explicit opt-in so I cannot do it by accident."
- **Future on-call session** — "As an agent diagnosing a dead proxy, I want a documented signature
  that tells me this failure happened in seconds, so that I restart correctly instead of
  re-investigating."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Server survives the launcher's process-group death.** By default
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` performs all of its synchronous validation (port free, provider API
  keys resolved, config readable, restart/cleanup phases) and then launches uvicorn in its **own**
  session/process group (`setsid`, with a `nohup … &` + `disown` fallback when `setsid` is
  unavailable), redirecting the child's stdout/stderr to a log file (`--log-file <path>`, default
  `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`) so the caller's pipe is **not** held open. It prints a single handoff
  line (child PID, log path, health-check command) and exits 0.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit foreground opt-in.** `--foreground` (or `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` for
  unattended callers that cannot pass flags) keeps today's blocking `exec` behaviour for interactive
  debugging. The flag is parsed and consumed by the script (never forwarded to uvicorn) and is
  documented in the usage header. Without it, foreground execution is not possible.
- [ ] **AC3 — Regression test for the failure mode.** A test asserts the launched server survives
  `SIGKILL` of the launching shell's entire process group: it starts the script in its own pgid,
  waits until the fake server binds an ephemeral port, `kill -9 -<launcher-pgid>`, then asserts the
  listener still answers. Sandboxed per the existing pattern (copy of the script, fake `python3`
  that stands in for uvicorn, isolated `$HOME`, stubbed `ss`/`netstat`, ephemeral port) so the live
  proxy, port 8000, llama-server and TTS are never touched, and it runs in the default suite.
- [ ] **AC4 — Docs: never start in the foreground under an agent tool call.**
  `/skill:start-proxy` (`.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`) and `proxy/README.md` state explicitly,
  in the start/restart section, that the proxy must never be started in the foreground under an
  agent tool call and show the exact detached command to use, plus the `--foreground` escape hatch
  and its `--log-file` companion.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs: diagnostic signature.** Documentation lists the signature of this failure so a
  future session recognises it immediately: proxy log ends abruptly with **no `Shutting down`
  line**, the triggering tool result reads `Command timed out after <N> seconds`, the launcher was
  run in the foreground, and sibling services (llama-server/TTS) are still alive. It also records
  the correct recovery (`/skill:start-proxy --restart`, warm llama-server preserved).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing callers and harnesses unaffected.** The already-detached call patterns
  (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &` in the skill and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh`, and `--restart`'s `pkill`/port-release logic) keep working,
  and the existing shell harnesses (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`,
  `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh`,
  `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh`) are updated with `--foreground` where they
  intentionally intercept the final `exec`, or otherwise still pass.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including script
  comments, `proxy/README.md`, the start-proxy skill, and any relevant runbook entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the uvicorn command line, config resolution, API-key fail-closed behaviour, restart
  gate or `--keep-llama-server` semantics — this is a launch-harness change only.
- Detaching must **not** inherit the caller's stdout/stderr pipe: inheriting it means `… | tail -20`
  still blocks the tool call until timeout and re-creates the original failure.
- Startup failures after the handoff (bind errors, model load failures, import errors) can no longer
  be reported through the launcher's exit code; callers must poll `/health`. The start-proxy skill
  already does this, and the handoff line must point at the log for the failure text.
- `setsid` and `nohup` must both be tolerated; no new dependency beyond coreutils.
- Tests must never touch the live proxy, ports 8000/8080/8081, or kill unrelated processes
  (project rule: never blanket-kill `python3`/`uvicorn`).

## Existing state

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` parses `--restart`, `--reason`, `--keep-llama-server`, `--verbose`,
  `--use-env-keys`, `--port`, does all validation, then `exec`s uvicorn inline — no detach, no
  `--foreground`, no log-file option, no PID file.
- Callers already background it externally: `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`
  (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &`) and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh:77`. Nothing prevents a foreground run, and
  `proxy/README.md` §Verbose documents `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --verbose` as the
  "recommended" invocation (a foreground command) without any warning.
- Sandboxed shell-test harness pattern already exists
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`): script copy + fake `python3`
  intercepting `-m uvicorn` + isolated `$HOME` + stubbed port probes + ephemeral port. The detach
  test can reuse it.
- Related history: backgrounded starts were killed in an earlier investigation
  (LP-0MQIWGJ6L000SA29) but that root cause was the test host, not a tool timeout.

## Desired change

1. Add `--foreground` / `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` and `--log-file <path>` to the flag parser
   (consumed, never forwarded to uvicorn).
2. Replace the final `exec` with a launch helper: after all validation, if foreground was requested,
   keep today's `exec`; otherwise `setsid` a re-execution of the same script in a child session with
   the uvicorn command, stdio redirected to the log file, then print the handoff line and exit 0.
   The re-exec must pass `--foreground` and **drop `--restart`** (the kill/cleanup and port-release
   phases already ran in the launcher) so the child cannot re-enter the detach path or repeat the
   restart storm.
3. New sandboxed detach test (AC3) plus harness updates for `--foreground` where needed.
4. Documentation: skill + README foreground warning, exact detached command, and the failure
   signature/recovery entry.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — flag parsing (`--foreground`, `--log-file`,
  `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND`), detach wrapper around the final exec, handoff line, usage header.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` — **new** AC3 regression test (pgid SIGKILL survival,
  sandboxed, fake uvicorn that binds an ephemeral port and records its pid/pgid).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` — add `--foreground` to invocations that intercept the final exec.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — never-foreground warning, exact detached command,
  `--log-file`, failure signature + recovery row in the Errors table.
- `proxy/README.md` — start section, §Verbose invocation guidance, diagnostic signature.

## Related work

- **LP-0MQMC3RQ1000ZY4M** — *Hardening: start-proxy.sh and proxy startup failures* (completed): the
  same script's interpreter/port/PYTHONPATH hardening; this item is the next robustness gap in the
  same launch path.
- **LP-0MQIWGJ6L000SA29** — *Investigate proxyctl restart integration flakiness (background start
  killed)* (completed): backgrounded starts killed in the **test host**; distinct root cause, but
  it established the `nohup`/`setsid` reasoning and the sandboxed harness habit re-used here.
- **LP-0MVD2RF7H008B7OT / LP-0MVF7DRMK001NHT8** — stale-key detection + its shell tests: the
  harness whose fake-`python3` interception the detach test re-uses and which needs `--foreground`.
- **LP-0MVJX7NGN006S74K** — *llama-server restart signature ignores models.ini and start-llama.sh
  changes* (open, unrelated area, same script): touch points overlap in `start-proxy.sh`; implement
  sequentially to avoid conflicting edits.
- **LP-0MNSRGEQW000QM7B / LP-0MPY3DG43009V6LO** — proxyctl start/restart CLI (completed): the
  external wrapper that already backgrounds the script; the new default must not double-detach-break
  it.

Potentially related docs:
- `proxy/README.md` (§Verbose, §Production/start) — documents the foreground invocation that this
  item must stop recommending.
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — the canonical agent start/restart procedure.
- `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh` — already-detached caller to regression-check.
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md` and `proxy/scripts/diagnose-llama-proxy-startup.sh` — existing
  diagnosis surfaces that could host the failure signature.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: silent startup failure.** Detaching hides post-launch uvicorn failures from the exit code.
  Mitigation: keep every existing pre-launch validation synchronous, print the log path in the
  handoff line, and document health polling (already the skill's contract).
- **Risk: pipe inheritance re-creates the bug.** If the detached child keeps the caller's stdout,
  `… | tail -20` blocks until the tool timeout again. Mitigation: AC1 mandates redirecting child
  stdio to the log file.
- **Risk: harness churn.** Sandboxed shell tests assert on the intercepted exec's stdout; they need
  `--foreground`. Mitigation: AC6 keeps them green (behaviour change is explicit, not silent).
- **Risk: child re-enters the detach path or repeats `--restart`.** A naive re-exec of the same
  argv would detach again (or sleep through the restart phases a second time). Mitigation: the
  re-exec is generated explicitly with `--foreground` and without `--restart`, plus a regression
  assertion in the detach test that the fake server is launched exactly once.
- **Risk: double backgrounding** (skill already uses `nohup … &` around a now self-detaching script)
  causes a stale expectation of "script still running". Mitigation: handoff line + exit 0 makes the
  new contract explicit; the skill's command is simplified.
- **Assumption:** self-detach-by-default (with `--foreground` opt-in) is preferred over
  "document-and-warn only", because it makes the failure impossible for every caller (agents, cron,
  ad-hoc shells) instead of depending on discipline. Recorded for producer confirmation.
- **Assumption:** the default log path is `/tmp/proxy-startup.log` (matches the current skill and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh` convention).
- **Scope-creep guard:** a PID file, systemd unit, or richer `proxyctl` integration are *not* in
  scope; record them as follow-up items if they surface during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (AC1 variant):** Should the script self-detach by default with an explicit `--foreground`
  opt-in, or stay foreground-only with only a documented warning? **Recommended:** self-detach by
  default — a warning cannot prevent an agent tool timeout from killing the server.
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** self-detach by default +
  `--foreground` / `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` opt-in, as specified in AC1/AC2. Source: work item
  description's AC1 explicitly permits either variant; agent selected the stronger one. Research:
  inspected all callers (`grep -rn "start-proxy" --include=*.sh --include=*.md`), all but the README
  already background it externally, so self-detaching is additive.
- **Q2 (log destination):** Where should the detached child's output go — inherit the caller's
  stdout, or a file? **Recommended:** a file (`--log-file`, default `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`).
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** a file, because inheriting the
  caller's pipe keeps `| tail -20` blocked and reproduces the original timeout. Source: incident
  evidence in the work item (the failing invocation was piped to `tail -20`).
- **Q3 (test placement/scope):** Should the pgid-survival test be opt-in (`LIVE_*` gated) or part of
  the default suite? **Recommended:** default suite, sandboxed.
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** default suite, because the harness
  pattern in `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` already isolates everything (fake interpreter, stubbed
  port probes, isolated `$HOME`, ephemeral port), so no live service is touched. Opt-in gating is
  reserved for tests that spawn/kill real OS listeners against real ports
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_restart.sh`).
- **Q4 (issue type/priority):** Item was filed as `chore`/`medium`. **Recommended:** `bug`/`high`
  (the change alters launch behaviour, and a dead proxy blocks every consumer).
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** reclassified to `bug` (the launch
  path demonstrably leaves the service dead) with `high` priority (a dead proxy blocks every
  consumer). Producer may override.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** – proxyctl: restart command (completed)
- **LP-0MQVJ76WP009QOUE** – TTS Server Lifecycle Management (completed)
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)

### Repository file matches
_No credible file matches: the automated sweep matched AC-id tokens (ac1..ac8) in a
vendored prompt-dataset fixture. The hand-curated **Related work** section above is
authoritative._
data.title: Harden proxy start against foreground invocation being killed by tool-call timeouts

data.description:
## Problem statement

Four offline analysis/benchmark scripts still hard-code the **retired fast/cheap
mode-profile** routing constants (warm clamps 83285 / 100000, cheap cold 42000,
breach caps 83285 / 61440, slot pools 3 / 2). Since LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 the live
single unified profile resolves to `warm=120000`, `cold=38000`, `slots=2`,
physical clamp `126976`, and since LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA there is no mode axis at
all — so new `routing_check` logs (`warm_threshold=120000`) fall into no known
bucket and every per-mode cap report is meaningless.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / analyst (Richard)** — runs these scripts over proxy logs to size
  compaction, hard caps and slot geometry. Needs bucket and breach numbers that
  reflect the config actually in force, and that stay reproducible over historical
  log windows.

### Example user stories

- As an analyst, I can run `analyze_context_distribution.py` over the last 7 days and
  get session buckets and breach counts for the **current** warm cap (120000) without
  editing constants first.
- As an analyst, re-running the script over the 2026-08-24..26 window still produces
  its historical (`83285` / `100000`) buckets, so old evaluations remain reproducible.
- As an analyst, `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` classifies prefills against the same
  thresholds the router uses (`cold 38000`, `warm 120000`, clamp `126976`, 2 slots),
  so its "above cap" counts match live behaviour.
- As a maintainer, changing the warm cap in `proxy/config.yaml` never again requires
  an edit-and-hope sweep through analysis scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No hard-coded routing thresholds in analysis/benchmark tooling.**
   `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
   `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` and
   `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` derive their cold/warm/breach/slot
   values from `proxy/config.yaml` (or from a single shared pure resolver — see
   Constraint C2). Grep proves it: no literal `83285`, `100000`, `42000`, `61440` or
   `87381` remains as a default in those files.
2. **Current live values are produced, and historical logs still classify.**
   With the shipped config the scripts resolve `cold=38000`, `warm=120000`,
   physical clamp `126976`, `slots=2`; a `routing_check` sample carrying
   `warm_threshold=120000` lands in the current bucket (not `other`), while samples
   from older logs (`83285`, `100000`) still bucket by their **observed**
   `warm_threshold` value rather than collapsing into `other`.
3. **`evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` MODES matches the live unified profile.**
   The fast/cheap mode split is replaced by (or collapses to) one profile with
   `cold_cache_threshold=38000`, `warm_cache_threshold_config=120000`,
   `session_slot_pool_size=2`, `local_model_ctx_size=262144`,
   `routing_clamp=126976` — or the config-derived equivalents — and
   `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` (which currently asserts
   `warm_threshold(fast) == 83285` / `== 100000`) is updated to assert the derived
   values and the new prefill-bucket boundaries.
4. **Tests cover the regression.** Both test modules
   (`proxy/tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py`) assert against a config fixture,
   including a `warm_threshold=120000` case and a legacy `83285`/`100000` case, so a
   future cap change in `config.yaml` cannot silently desynchronise the tooling.
5. **No production behaviour change.** No file under `proxy/proxy/` changes routing
   behaviour (a pure-helper extraction, if taken, must be a behaviour-preserving move
   covered by the existing suite); docstrings/help text that describe the old mode
   profiles are corrected.
6. **Docs updated** — `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/README.md`,
   `docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md` and any script docstrings that
   quote the retired mode thresholds now describe the unified-profile derivation.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **C1 — offline only.** None of these scripts is on the production routing path; a
  fix must not touch routing decisions, `provider.py` logic, or `config.yaml` values.
- **C2 — dependency weight.** The analysis scripts are deliberately stdlib-only and
  are imported directly by tests (`import analyze_context_distribution`). Importing
  `proxy.proxy.provider` would drag in `fastapi`/`httpx`; therefore prefer extracting
  the *pure* resolvers (`effective_per_slot_threshold`, warm/cold/slot/ctx getters,
  `effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`) into a stdlib-only module
  (e.g. `proxy/proxy/routing_thresholds.py`) that both `provider.py` and the scripts
  import. If the extraction proves invasive, a script-local `yaml`-based resolution
  that reuses the same formula is acceptable **provided** it is the only copy and is
  test-pinned against the live config — duplicating the formula in three scripts is
  not acceptable (it is how this defect arose).
- **C3 — historical reproducibility.** Aug-2026 evaluation artifacts
  (`proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/distribution.{json,md}`) were produced with the
  old clamps; re-running over the same window must still yield those buckets.
- **C4 — CLI compatibility.** `--fast-cap` / `--cheap-cap` / `--mode fast|cheap` flags
  may be retired, but any removal must be documented in the docstring/help text and
  should not break the documented invocation examples.
- **C5 — repo boundaries.** No edits to `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` in this
  item even though it carries mode-aware report logic; that skill already resolves
  per-mode triggers from config (`reporting.py:_mode_trigger`) and is not stale in the
  same way.

## Existing state

Live `proxy/config.yaml` (unified profile, mode overlays removed):

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `local_model_ctx_size` | 262144 |
| `session_slot_pool_size` | 2 |
| `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` | 38000 |
| `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` | 120000 |
| `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` | 0.4578 → ceiling 120010, capped to 120000 |
| physical per-slot clamp | `262144 // 2 - 4096` = **126976** |
| effective warm | `min(120000, 126976)` = **120000** (matches logged `warm_threshold=120000`) |

Stale constants found:

| file | symbol | value | live equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` | `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD` | 83285 | 120000 (only profile) |
| " | `CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` | 100000 | — (mode retired) |
| " | `FAST_CAP` | 83285 | 120000 |
| " | `CHEAP_CAP` | 61440 | — (mode retired) |
| `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` | `FAST_CAP`, `CHEAP_CAP` | 83285, 61440 | as above |
| `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` | `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`, `CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` + `Mode.from_warm_threshold` | 83285, 100000 | 120000 |
| `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` | `MODES["fast"]` | cold 38000, warm 100000, slots 3, clamp 83285 | cold 38000, warm 120000, slots 2, clamp 126976 |
| " | `MODES["cheap"]` | cold 42000, warm 100000, slots 2, clamp 100000 | (collapse to the unified profile) |

Existing single-source-of-truth helpers already in the proxy:
`provider.effective_per_slot_threshold`, `provider.effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`,
`provider.compute_hard_routing_cap` (mode argument retained but the per-mode ratios are
retired), `provider._effective_large_context_thresholds(config) -> (cold, warm)`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one stdlib-only resolver module (or reuse an existing light one) that
   maps `config.yaml` → `(cold, warm, physical_clamp, slots, ctx_size, hard_cap)`
   using the shipped 3-term warm model, and make `provider.py` import the pure
   functions from it (behaviour-preserving move, no logic change).
2. Point all four scripts at that resolver. Replace the mode-bucket heuristic with
   **observed-value bucketing**: bucket/label each session by the `warm_threshold`
   value in its own log lines (e.g. `warm=120000`, `warm=83285`), and compute breach
   counts against the resolved cap for the *current* config by default, with a
   `--warm-cap`/`--cold-cap` override for historical replay. `warm_threshold=120000`
   must therefore be a first-class bucket, and the `other` fallback only catches
   genuinely unknown values.
3. Collapse `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.MODES` to a single profile derived from config;
   keep the `--mode` flag only if it remains meaningful (otherwise retire it and say so
   in the docstring). Update the two test modules accordingly.
4. Correct every docstring/help string that still describes the fast/cheap mode
   profiles as live.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/routing_thresholds.py` — New (or equivalent): stdlib-only pure resolvers for effective cold/warm/clamp/slots from a config dict, extracted from `provider.py`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Import the pure resolvers from the new module (behaviour-preserving; no logic change).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — Drop the four hard-coded constants; resolve thresholds from config; replace mode bucketing with observed-`warm_threshold` bucketing; correct the docstring's "Mode classification" section.
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` — Drop its duplicated `FAST_CAP`/`CHEAP_CAP`; use the shared resolver and the same bucket keys as the analyser.
- `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` — Drop `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`/`CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` and the `Mode.from_warm_threshold` table.
- `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` — Replace `MODES` fast/cheap entries with the single config-derived profile (`cold 38000`, `warm 120000`, slots 2, clamp 126976).
- `proxy/tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py` — Assert config-derived thresholds plus a `warm_threshold=120000` case and legacy 83285/100000 cases.
- `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` — Replace the pinned `83285`/`100000` assertions with derived values and new bucket boundaries.
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_thresholds.py` — New: pin the extracted resolver against the shipped `config.yaml` values (cold 38000, warm 120000, clamp 126976).
- `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/README.md` — Update the script description and invocation examples (no `--fast-cap`/`--cheap-cap` mode wording).
- `docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md` — Update the mode-constant description to the unified profile.

## Related work

- LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 — Raise local warm-context routing cap 100K → 120K (and the economic-ceiling ratio that binds it). *Origin of the drift; completed.*
- LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA — Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode (epic, completed). *Retired the mode axis these scripts still model.*
- LP-0MTVXP7DG00613ZB — Unified `compaction_trigger_ratio` / retirement of `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_fast`.
- LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN — 3-term warm model (`min(physical clamp, economic ceiling)`); the formula the resolver must reuse.
- LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 — Physical per-slot clamp (`ctx_size // slots - 4096`).
- LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B — F1 session context-size distribution analysis (author of `analyze_context_distribution.py`).
- LP-0MTAQNAIH001RN1S — Hard local-routing cap evaluation (author of `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py`).
- LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S — Implement hard local-routing cap (fast 70K / cheap 61.4K) + cheap compaction gate. *Origin of the `61440` cheap cap these scripts still quote.*
- LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43 — Revert hard-routing cap to dynamic (disable 70K/61.4K caps). *Superseded the absolute caps; the analysis scripts never followed.*
- LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP — Geometry A/B protocol and reporter (open): also manipulates `session_slot_pool_size` and warm/cold thresholds; will want the same resolver.
- LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN — Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (open): its arm geometry will invalidate any hard-coded constants again — reinforces deriving from config.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — silent formula duplication.** Fixing the numbers by editing literals satisfies AC2 but recreates the defect at the next cap change. *Mitigation:* AC1's grep check + AC4's config-fixture tests.
- **R2 — provider refactor risk.** Extracting resolvers out of `provider.py` touches production code for a tooling defect. *Mitigation:* pure move only, no logic change, full suite gate; fall back to a script-local `yaml` resolver (C2) if the move destabilises `provider.py`.
- **R3 — historical comparability.** Observed-value bucketing changes bucket *labels* (`fast`/`cheap` → `warm=<n>`), so old and new artifacts are not byte-comparable. *Mitigation:* documented in the script docstring and README; the `--warm-cap`/`--cold-cap` overrides preserve old numbers on demand.
- **R4 — scope creep.** Other stale mode references certainly exist elsewhere (e.g. `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` report text, docs prose beyond the two files above). *Mitigation:* C5 keeps the skill out of scope; file follow-ups as `discovered-from` items rather than expanding this low-priority chore.
- **A1 (assumption).** The fast/cheap mode axis is genuinely retired, so collapsing to a single unified profile is correct; the mode labels are not to be preserved as a *config* concept. Evidence: `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` ("mode overlays … were removed"), `provider.py` (`compute_hard_routing_cap` uses the unified profile unconditionally), `config.yaml` (only `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_fast` marked RETIRED, single slot pool/slot thresholds).
- **A2 (assumption).** `correlate_oversized_sessions.py` and `run_compaction_experiment.py` are in scope even though the seed text named only two scripts: they carry the same constants and one imports the analyser's helpers, so fixing only the named two would leave the same defect one file away. Recorded here rather than as a blocker.
- **A3 (assumption).** `PyYAML` may be used by the scripts if the pure-helper extraction is rejected, because `proxy/requirements.txt` pins `pyyaml>=6.0` and the scripts run in the proxy venv.
- **A4 (assumption).** No operator-facing behaviour depends on the scripts' `--mode`/`--fast-cap` flag names; retiring them is acceptable with documented help text.
- **No production backlog impact:** priority `low` (analysis tooling only, no live behaviour affected) is retained.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed description supplied a concrete problem statement, two named files and
three acceptance criteria; repo search answered every remaining question, so no
operator interview was required.

- Q: Which config values are live today? — Answer (repo): `session_slot_pool_size: 2`,
  `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, cold 38000, warm 120000, ratio 0.4578 → effective
  warm `min(120000, 262144//2-4096=126976) = 120000`. Source: `proxy/config.yaml`
  (lines ~1261, ~1296, ~1395, ~1649), `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  `_effective_large_context_thresholds`.
- Q: Is the fast/cheap mode axis dead, i.e. should the fix collapse to one profile? —
  Answer: yes (assumption A1). Source: `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` header
  ("mode overlays … were removed"), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (completed epic).
- Q: Are there more stale copies than the two named scripts? — Answer: yes, two more —
  `correlate_oversized_sessions.py` (`FAST_CAP`/`CHEAP_CAP`) and
  `run_compaction_experiment.py` (`FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`/`CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` +
  `Mode.from_warm_threshold`). Source: `grep -rn '83285\|100000\|61440' proxy/scripts
  proxy/benchmarks`. Added to scope under assumption A2.
- Q: Can the scripts import the proxy's resolver directly? — Answer: not cleanly —
  `provider.py` imports `httpx`/`fastapi` while the analysis scripts are stdlib-only
  and are imported bare by tests. Hence constraint C2 (extract pure helpers, or a
  single script-local resolver) and risk R2.
- Q: Must historical eval windows still reproduce? — Answer: yes (constraint C3), so
  bucket by the observed `warm_threshold` value rather than only by the current config
  (assumption/R3, AC2).

- **LP-0MTVPJBF0001SQF4** – Cap empty-response cooldown at 10s instead of exponential backoff (completed)

## Problem statement

Between the 24 h window anchored on 2026-10-18/19 and the window anchored on 2026-10-20/21, logged (paid-serving) token volume rose **+96%** (421.7 M → 828.5 M) while requests *fell* 29% (12,810 → 9,137) — i.e. ≈32.9 k → ≈90.7 k tokens per request (≈2.8×). Nothing owns that trend: the verification item that surfaced it (LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO) could only show the off-peak low-priority fallback epic did **not** cause it. Until the growth is attributed, we cannot tell an intended context-growth change from a context-budget/compaction regression or a token-accounting artefact, and we have no standing metric that would have flagged it.

## Users

- **Producer / cost owner** — needs to know whether paid-serving spend doubled for a legitimate reason (bigger sessions) or because of a regression, and needs the answer recorded where the verification record lives.
- **Proxy maintainer** — needs any regression found here either fixed with a regression test or filed as a blocking child with numbers attached, and needs the failing mechanism named (compaction, context budget, token accounting).
- **Operator reading the daily proxy-usage report** — needs a durable per-request cost signal so the next drift is visible on the day it happens instead of via an ad-hoc before/after comparison.

Example user stories:

- As the cost owner, I want the +96% rise attributed to a named cause with numbers, so I can decide whether the paid tier is behaving as designed.
- As a proxy maintainer, I want a `provider_context_exceeded`/accounting check that distinguishes re-attribution from real extra tokens, so I do not chase a phantom regression.
- As the report operator, I want tokens-per-request on the daily report, so a 2.8× shift is caught automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The candidate causes (genuine context growth, context-budget/compaction regression, token-accounting artefact, serving-tier mix) are each ruled in or out with a quantified two-window comparison — `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages` and `duration_seconds` distributions from `standard_sessions.csv` / `low_priority_sessions.csv`, plus per-serving-entry token triples (`tokens=prompt/completion/total`) and per-dispatch `routing_check ... estimated_tokens` distributions.
- AC2: The tokens-per-request increase is attributed to a named cause with supporting numbers, or explicitly recorded as unexplained with the residual quantified (e.g. "X% of the +407 M explained by context growth, Y M unattributed").
- AC3: Any regression found is either fixed here with a regression test, or filed as a child work item with the blocking relationship recorded (`wl dep add`/comment `Blocks:` / `Blocked-by:`).
- AC4: A durable cost metric is implemented (preferred) or, if deferred, proposed as a concrete child item: tokens-per-request (and per-session token totals) surfaced in the daily proxy-usage report with the trend visible across days.
- AC5: Findings are commented on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO so the verification record carries the resolution.
- AC6 (testing/validation): Any metric or parser change ships with meaningful tests (aggregation unit tests over fixture sessions plus an `analyze_proxy_usage.py` end-to-end assertion), and every number quoted in the findings is reproducible from a committed command.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, and `proxy/docs/routing.md` if a routing/budget mechanism is implicated).
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Log retention.** Both windows are still resolvable from rotated logs in `/var/log/llama-proxy` (verified 2026-10-22: `proxy.log-2026-10-18_00.gz` … `proxy.log.2026-10-21_14.gz` cover both windows), but retention is not contractual — measure early or archive the two windows under `/tmp` before they rotate away (the `/tmp/cost/*` outputs cited in the description no longer exist and must be regenerated).
- **Only paid streams carry tokens.** Local and `munitoai-free` streams emit no `tokens=` triple, so "logged tokens" are paid-serving tokens by construction; free-tier share must be read from stream **counts**, never tokens. Any conclusion must state which population it is about.
- **Confounded windows.** The post window contains a proxy restart (2026-10-20 13:10 local) and the context-budget/admission commit series (`c443240c`, `f496626e`, `42f93580`, `ec5514fc`, `242d03f4`, `6999492a`, `a8b56995`) plus `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events) which did not exist pre-change. Single-window before/after cannot separate co-landed changes; use a third reference window and/or per-day series where a cause is ambiguous.
- **Analysis is deterministic only.** Use `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`; do not hand-roll log parsing, and do not edit log data.
- **Investigation scope.** This is an analysis task: fix only a regression that is small and well-understood; larger remediation is filed as a child (AC3).

## Existing state

Measured with the proxy-usage-analysis CLI (log clock = local Europe/Dublin, UTC+1):

| Metric | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions / requests | 217 / 12,810 | 228 / 9,137 | −29% requests |
| Logged tokens (input+output) | 421.7 M | 828.5 M | **+96%** |
| Tokens per request | ≈32.9 k | ≈90.7 k | **≈2.8×** |
| Token share by serving entry | `opencode-go-3` 99.98%, `-2` 0.02% | `-3` 99.36%, `-2` 0.20%, `deepseek-flash` 0.44% | — |
| Local streams | 910 | 576 | −37% |
| `munitoai-free` + `munitoai` entry lines | 14,555 | 5,967 | −59% |

Known-relevant capabilities already in the codebase:

- `AnalysisResult.total_tokens()` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` already sums `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the `Stream finished ... tokens=prompt/completion/total` lines — the fetch for per-request normalisation exists, but **no report section divides by request count** (checked: no `tokens_per_request` symbol anywhere in the analysis scripts).
- `SessionStats` already records `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `avg_response_size`, `messages` per session, and `CSV_COLUMNS` in `reporting.py` publishes them — so AC1's distribution check needs no new instrumentation.
- `compaction_events` are already collected by the parser (LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT), so compaction activity can be compared across windows without new parsing.
- Per-dispatch prompt size is already logged: `routing_check ... estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=… cached_ratio=… cache_state=… messages=…` (entry-level, independent of sessions) — e.g. 2,892 `routing_check` lines in the 2026-10-18/19/20 rotated segments sampled vs 7,016 in the 2026-10-20/21 segments. This is the lowest-cost direct test of "prompts got bigger" and needs no new instrumentation.
- Candidate regression surface, from the commit series above: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (context budget/cached-ratio/prefix bootstrap), `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`, `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`.

## Desired change

1. Regenerate both windows (and at least one additional reference day, e.g. 2026-10-19/20 and 2026-10-22) with the analysis CLI into a stable output dir; archive the CSVs so the numbers are reproducible after rotation.
2. Measure per-dispatch prompt size from `routing_check` lines (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `cache_state`, `messages`) for each window — this separates "bigger prompts" from "more dispatches per request" without depending on session boundaries.
3. Compare distributions of `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages`, `duration_seconds` and per-session token totals across windows; decompose the +407 M delta into (a) more sessions, (b) bigger per-session context, (c) more tokens re-sent per request, (d) **tier mix** — free/local share per request fell from 1.14 to 0.65 `munitoai*` lines per request, so part of the paid-token rise may be traffic re-attributed from the free tier to paid entries rather than a per-request increase — and (e) other/unexplained.
4. Check the accounting hypothesis against `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events): confirm each event maps to at most one stream's token triple and that no tokens are counted twice or re-attributed from the free tier.
5. Check the compaction hypothesis: compaction event rate per session across windows, and whether post-compaction prompts grew (i.e. compaction shrinking less or being bypassed).
6. Write the verdict into a comment on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO with the decomposition table; fix or file the regression (AC3).
7. **Preferred AC4 implementation**: add a tokens-per-request (and total/median per-session token) metric to the analysis report — an `AnalysisResult`/report addition plus a `## Cost / token volume` style section and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Needs a tokens-per-request aggregate (total input+output ÷ request count) and per-window token trend helper.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Needs the report section rendering the token-volume / tokens-per-request metric and the CSV columns it depends on.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — Needs CLI wiring only if the metric is exposed as a flag/output.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — Needs unit tests for the new aggregate plus an end-to-end report assertion on fixture logs.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` — Needs the new metric documented.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` / `proxy/config.yaml` — Only if the cause lands in context budget, cached-ratio prefix credit or compaction handling; fix + regression test under `proxy/tests/`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — Only if a routing/budget mechanism is implicated.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO** — *Verify off-peak low-priority fallback in a live window* (completed): the verification that surfaced the trend; AC5 requires the resolution be recorded there.
- **LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX** — off-peak low-priority fallback epic (the change the verification was testing; not the cause, but the baseline window definition comes from it).
- **LP-0MVF9N3BV00155RI** — *F4: Docs and observability* — introduced the `provider_context_exceeded` observability whose accounting is candidate cause 3.
- **LP-0MVF9N2QL001CDA7** / **LP-0MVF9MY0W002J2N3** — `max_context_tokens` gate implementation and per-entry context-limit tests: the context-budget surface that candidate cause 2 may implicate.
- **LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ** — *Design experiment: validate session compaction gains without quality loss* — relevant to the compaction hypothesis (whether compaction shrinks prompts efficiently).
- **LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B** — *Analyze session context-size distributions from 2026-08-24→26 reports* (completed): direct precedent for AC1 — median/mean/p90/p95/max of session context sizes plus breach counts and trend analysis. Reuse its method rather than inventing one.
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** — *Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File* (completed): relevant to the accounting-artefact hypothesis — a logging gap would distort logged-token volume.
- **Potentially related docs:** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md`, `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`.

Changes that landed inside the post window (verified commit → item mapping):

| Commit | Work item | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `c443240c` | LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ | Prefill-ETA admission guard: stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget |
| `f496626e` | LP-0MVGDUVS6003T2IX | Re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated) |
| `42f93580` | LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ | Serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU |
| `ec5514fc` | LP-0MVGGI4Y0003K4AZ | Increase `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` to 3 (tier-mix candidate) |
| `242d03f4` | LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 | Raise local warm-context routing cap 100K → 120K (and the economic-ceiling ratio) |
| `6999492a` | LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV | Second-turn `cached_ratio` scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn |
| `a8b56995` | LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP | Local dispatch starves returning sessions: contention queue causes local↔remote churn |

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)
- **LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B** – Analyze session context-size distributions from 2026-08-24→26 reports (completed)
- **LP-0MSNM9BDV007DQXB** – Wire /admin/sessions to index-backed listing (bounded) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)

> Triage of the automated section: the three work items are legitimate (listed above); the three repository "matches" are false positives — they match boilerplate AC tokens (`ac1`…`ac5`) inside a calibration dataset, not this item's subject. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVIAEARO0001O7R.md`.

## Evidence commands

```bash
# both windows, regenerated and archived (the /tmp/cost/* copies from the discovery pass are gone)
for w in "2026-10-18 14:37:48|2026-10-19 14:37:48|base24" \
         "2026-10-19 14:44:27|2026-10-20 14:44:27|ref24" \
         "2026-10-20 14:44:27|2026-10-21 14:44:27|post24"; do
  IFS='|' read -r s e name <<<"$w"
  python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "$s" --end "$e" --output-dir "$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/$name"
done

# context/message distributions per window
python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, statistics as s
for name in ("base24", "ref24", "post24"):
    p = f"/home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/cost/{name}/standard_sessions.csv"
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(p)))
    for col in ("start_context_size", "max_context_size", "messages", "duration_seconds"):
        vals = [int(float(r[col])) for r in rows if r.get(col)]
        print(name, col, len(vals), round(s.median(vals)), round(s.mean(vals)))
PY

# accounting check: per-entry token triples and provider_context_exceeded events
zcat /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_15.gz /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_21.gz \
    /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log-2026-10-21_00.gz /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-21_07.gz \
  | grep "^.*entry=opencode-go" | grep -o "tokens=[0-9]*/[0-9]*/[0-9]*" | head

grep -ch "provider_context_exceeded" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | paste -sd+ | bc

# per-dispatch prompt size (independent of session boundaries)
zcat /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-2[01]_*.gz | grep -o "routing_check .*estimated_tokens=[0-9]*" \
  | grep -o "estimated_tokens=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2 | sort -n \
  | awk '{s+=$1; a[NR]=$1} END{print "n="NR, "median="a[int(NR/2)], "mean="int(s/NR)}'
```

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — co-landed changes.** Seven commits plus a proxy restart sit inside the post window; a single before/after pair cannot attribute cleanly. Mitigation: add reference windows and a per-day trend; if attribution stays ambiguous, AC2's "unexplained with residual" branch is the honest outcome.
- **Risk — log loss.** Rotated logs are not guaranteed; measurements must be archived. Mitigation: run the CLI early and copy CSVs into the work-item comment/summary.
- **Risk — scope creep into proxy tuning.** Fixing every mechanism noticed would balloon the item. Mitigation: fix only small, well-understood regressions; file the rest as children (AC3).
- **Risk — tier-mix confounding.** The free-tier line share fell faster than requests (`munitoai*` lines per request 1.14 → 0.65), so part of the paid-token rise may be re-attribution rather than growth. Mitigation: decompose by tier before concluding (Desired change step 2d).
- **Risk — metric theatre.** A tokens-per-request number without a baseline/target will not catch drift. Mitigation: publish a per-day series (AC4) rather than a single scalar.
- **Assumption — "logged tokens" means paid-serving tokens.** Only opencode/deepseek streams emit `tokens=` triples; conclusions are scoped accordingly and free-tier share is reported from counts.
- **Assumption — both windows are still re-measurable** from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (verified 2026-10-22); if a window has rotated away, the recorded figures from the description are the fallback baseline and that limitation is stated.
- **Assumption — no operator-requested scope beyond the named candidates** was given; four-window/tier-mix comparison and the AC4 metric are the assumed floor. The serving-tier-mix candidate was added by the agent because the free-tier line count fell 59% against a 29% request drop; it is not a new requirement, only a fourth hypothesis for the same question.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (goal, two measured windows, named candidate causes, ACs, evidence commands) was sufficient to draft the brief.
- Assumption recorded (agent, not operator): AC4 is implemented in this item rather than merely proposed — the metric is small, lives in the existing analysis package, and is the only durable defence against a repeat. Source: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` already computes token totals, so the addition is a report/aggregate change.
- Assumption recorded (agent): "logged tokens" is treated as paid-serving tokens throughout; free-tier share read from entry counts. Source: `Stream finished ... tokens=prompt/completion/total` is emitted only for opencode/deepseek streams.
- Assumption recorded (agent): issue type stays `task` (investigation) at priority `medium`; reassign upward if a regression is confirmed.
