## Goal

Evaluate (with measurements, go/no-go) whether widening the **per-session KV snapshot pool** (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4, snapshots under `session_slot_save_path/slot_<id>.bin`) raises local prefix reuse for the small/medium working set — as the recommended alternative to adding live llama slots, which would shrink per-slot context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots) and exclude the long-context sessions that dominate this workload.

## Why

- Measured prefix reuse is poor: aggregate 26.1 %, median **15.6 %** for prompts >20k tokens (227 prompts), 28 fully cold; 27 distinct sessions cycled through a 2-slot pool in ~5.4 h.
- More live slots buy *residency*, not throughput (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills), and cost per-slot address space for a long-context workload.
- The snapshot mechanism already exists (per-session save/restore, `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds: 0.0015`, capped at `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds: 60`, pool capped by `session_slot_pool_size: 2`) but is degraded under load (`session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`, circuit-breaker cooldown). Restore cost estimate: ~50k tokens ≈ 75 s → capped 60 s, so the mechanism currently helps only the <40k band.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Benchmark:** measure save/restore latency (and disk footprint) per prompt-size band (10k / 25k / 40k / 60k+) on the production GPU host, including under load (another session streaming), against the 0.0015 s/token timeout model.
- **AC2 — Go/no-go with evidence:** with `session_slot_pool_size: 4` in a replay/bake-off on the 2026-10-24 thrash window (or equivalent fixture), report the reuse uplift (baseline 15.6 % median for >20k prompts) and the restore-success rate (skip_when_busy / cooldown exclusions).
- **AC3 — If go:** ship the config change plus retention/eviction semantics for 4 snapshots (pool eviction policy, disk cap, failure cooldowns unchanged) and any report/observability fields (restore-hit rate per session, snapshot pool occupancy) so the proxy-usage-analysis report can monitor the effect.
- **AC4 — If no-go:** record the measured blockers (latency, skip rate, restore failures) as a comment on this item so the decision is reproducible.
- **AC5 — No change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item** (that remains the separate 3-slot "fast" profile discussion).

## Tests

Bake-off harness replaying fixture logs + real save/restore micro-benchmark on the host; unit tests for pool-size > 2 retention semantics; report-schema tests for the new fields.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (slot-churn / tenancy investigation, option 3a of the recommendation).
- This is an evaluation/deliberation item, not a mandate to change configuration.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD** – Slot-count benchmark: find optimal session_slot_pool_size for Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MPOL5S7W007GRWB** – Include router model in slot save/restore requests (completed)
- **LP-0MU03AL730000B5W** – Slot counts: default and fast -> 1 slot, cheap -> 3 slots (completed)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)

## Goal

As the implementing agent for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, I need the failing-first unit
tests for the residency-aware admission ladder so that AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6 and AC7
(unit half) are pinned by executable, meaningful assertions before any production
code changes.

## Scope

New test module `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` plus extensions
to existing suites. Tests are written against the *intended* API (a shared residency
view + the admission ladder), so they are added with
`@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="pending LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 / LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA / LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI / LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M")` — the implement
skill's changed-scope gate therefore stays green, and the implementation items remove
the markers as each behaviour lands. No production code changes in this item.

Store-of-truth fixtures: a stubbed `_last_slot_details_cache` snapshot (slot_id,
is_processing, context_tokens, timestamp) and a stubbed `session._slot_owners` map.
No HTTP, no `/slots` call, no sleeps — every matrix cell is a pure function call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit coverage for: resident accept / non-resident reject, ratio boundary, tenancy bound, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder, predicted-vs-actual divergence, and both reclaim bounds (this item authors those tests first).
- **AC7 (unit) — resident accept / non-resident reject:** tests assert the ladder admits a large prompt when the session's measured `reuse_ratio` is at/above `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` and skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` when below it.
- **AC1 — ratio boundary:** a dedicated test asserts the exact boundary (`reuse_ratio == local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` admits; one token below rejects) and that `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0` disables the gate entirely.
- **AC1/AC7 — unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder:** tests cover (a) `context_tokens` known → measured ratio used, (b) `context_tokens` `None` but the session owns the slot → treated as resident (restore path), (c) neither → non-resident, falling back to today's predicted-ratio decision.
- **AC7 — predicted-vs-actual divergence:** a test pins the 2026-10-24 failure shape — predicted `cached_ratio` 0.99 with actual `n_past=738` of a 49,103-token prompt (actual reuse ≈ 0.015) must reject, proving the live measurement supersedes the sidecar prediction.
- **AC2 — tenancy bound:** tests assert at most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions hold a large-prompt local reservation, that a same-session re-entry is always permitted, and that the denial reason is `tenant_limit`.
- **AC6 — both reclaim bounds:** tests assert an observed disconnect releases the reservation within one ~10 s `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` cycle, and a silent half-open drop is released by the 180 s no-progress watchdog and never only at the 900 s lifetime ceiling.
- **AC3 — live-prefix pricing:** a test asserts `new_tokens` is priced from the live measurement, so a request whose live `new_tokens` exceeds the cold threshold is refused even when the predicted ratio says it is cheap.
- All new tests run through the test skill (`/skill:test`) and collect cleanly with the rest of `proxy/tests`.

## Implementation sketch

- Build a small fixture factory returning
  `(slot_snapshot, slot_owners, now)` and reuse it across all matrix cells.
- Parametrise the ladder matrix over (context_tokens known/unknown, owner yes/no,
  ratio above/below/at boundary, tenants 1/2/3, snapshot fresh/stale).
- Do not fake production internals: stub only the two documented sources
  (`_last_slot_details_cache`, `session._slot_owners`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_session_slot_affinity_continuity.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_cooldown.py`

## Dependencies

None — this is the test-first seed item; every implementation item depends on it.

## Assumptions

- `local_idle_admit_*` behaviour (`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`) must keep working, so the
  idle-exempt override is a test cell in this module (it stays last in the ladder).
- The 2026-10-24 divergence numbers (49,103-token prompt, `n_past=738`) are recorded
  in the parent item's problem statement and are usable as fixture constants.

## Decomposition (parent `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`)

Sibling items created by the plan session (2026-10-25). Execute in dependency order;
test items precede implementation items.

| Step | Item id | Scope | Depends on |
|------|---------|-------|------------|
| C1 | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H | Test harness (this item) | — |
| C2 | LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 | Shared residency view | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H |
| C3 | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA | Resident-prefix gate + live pricing | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 |
| C4 | LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI | Session tenancy bound | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 |
| C5 | LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M | Tenancy lease reclaim | LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI |
| C6 | LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM | Observability + usage report | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI |
| C7 | LP-0MVN4LB5W005WJ71 | Thrash-window replay test | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI, LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM |
| C8 | LP-0MVN4LBOQ00743MG | Documentation | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI, LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M |
| C9 | LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P | Rollout + AC4 arming | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80, LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI, LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M, LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM, LP-0MVN4LB5W005WJ71, LP-0MVN4LBOQ00743MG |

- `C1` is the test-first seed: its new-behaviour tests carry
  `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="pending <impl-item-id>")` so every commit
  stays green; the implementation item that lands each behaviour removes its markers.
- Shared constraint across all items: read the cached slot snapshot
  (`observability._last_slot_details_cache` + `session._slot_owners`), never issue a
  synchronous `/slots` call on the admission hot path (`LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`).
- Shared constraint across all items: no new logging convention — extend the
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` AC7 ERROR-level eviction event for eviction records.
- Cross-item budget: the 25k cold-prefill budget constant is owned by
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` and consumed, never redefined, here.

## Scope

New module `proxy/proxy/residency.py` exposing one function (e.g.
`get_residency_view(now=None) -> ResidencyView`) plus a small dataclass per slot.
It copies under a snapshot (never holds a lock across an await), records snapshot age
from the cache's own timestamp, and returns an explicit `unknown` state rather than
raising when the snapshot is missing/stale. `admission_reserve.py` consumes the same
view so `POST /llama/local/reserve` and the guard agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — residency view feeds the resident-prefix gate:** the view exposes, per slot, the owner session, `context_tokens` (possibly `None`), `is_processing` and the snapshot age; a unit test asserts the exact mapping from a stubbed `_last_slot_details_cache` + `_slot_owners` pair, including the multi-endpoint (`endpoint, slot_id`) key shape.
- **AC1 — no `/slots` call on the admission hot path:** a test asserts the view performs no `httpx` call and no `_query_slots_detail` invocation (monkeypatched to fail if called), honouring the `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC` constraint.
- **AC1 — fail-open on unknown state:** a missing snapshot, a snapshot older than the freshness bound, or a slot with unreported `context_tokens` is reported as `unknown` (never an exception, never a fabricated context size), so the admission ladder can fall back to the session-owns-slot check and then to today's predicted-ratio decision.
- **AC1 — no lock inversion:** the view is read from a copied snapshot, so a test asserts a slot-details refresh happening concurrently cannot mutate the view mid-decision and that no asyncio lock is held across an await in the view path.
- **AC5 — decision-shape support:** the view yields every field the admission logging needs (`n_past_actual`, `slot_owner_session`, snapshot age) so the observability item logs from it rather than re-deriving.
- All new tests run through the test skill; the item's own tests are green without `xfail` markers (the view is introduced here).

## Implementation sketch

- Read `_last_slot_details_cache` under a shallow copy of dicts; pair each slot with
  `_slot_owners[(endpoint, slot_id)]`; attach `age = now - snapshot_timestamp`.
- Add a module-level freshness bound constant (the snapshot is refreshed ~1 s by
  `_periodic_broadcast_loop()`; a stale bound of a few seconds keeps decisions honest
  while remaining fail-open).
- Keep it dependency-free: no new poller, no new task, no new config knob.

## Goal

As a multi-turn local session, my large prompt should only be admitted locally when
my resident prefix is actually reusable — and as the proxy operator, a cold prompt
that cannot finish inside the prefill deadline must not be admitted just because a
prediction said it would be cheap.

## Scope

Implement the admission ladder in `provider._should_skip_local()` (or its replacement
entry point) using the shared residency view: (i) unchanged hard
`warm_cache_threshold` cap; (ii) **resident-prefix gate** (AC1) with the fallback
ladder; (iii) tenancy check delegated to the tenancy item; (iv) cold pricing from the
live `new_tokens` (AC3); (v) the existing idle-exempt override stays **last** so an
idle GPU still serves cold work. The 25k budget constant itself is owned by
`LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` and is consumed, not redefined, here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Resident-prefix admission gate:** before a local dispatch of a large prompt is admitted, the router computes the session's *actual* reusable prefix from live slot state and admits only when `reuse_ratio = min(context_tokens, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens` is `>= local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` (default `0.5`, `0` disables). Otherwise it skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` and the chain falls through as it does today, so cold prompts above the admission budget from non-resident sessions are never admitted.
- **AC3 — Live-prefix pricing:** the cold-cache gate prices `new_tokens` from the same live measurement rather than the predicted sidecar ratio (`slot_cache_ratio.py`), so the new-token cap is evaluated against real prefill work; zero admissions occur with live `new_tokens` above the cold threshold unless idle-exempt.
- **AC1 — fallback ladder (fail-open):** `context_tokens` known → measured ratio; unknown but the session owns the slot → treated as resident (restore path); otherwise → non-resident, degrading to today's predicted-ratio decision. A missing/stale snapshot never produces a hard local outage.
- **Idle-awareness preserved:** `local_idle_admit_enabled` (`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`) still overrides the economic bypass for an idle GPU and remains the final rung of the ladder — a regression test asserts an idle local backend still admits cold work when the residency gate would otherwise decline.
- **No hot-path `/slots` call:** the gate consumes only the residency view; the `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC` constraint is re-asserted by a unit test.
- The unit tests from the test-harness item covering AC1/AC3 lose their `xfail` markers and pass; all tests run through the test skill.

## Implementation sketch

- Add `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` to `proxy/config.yaml` `server:` block
  (default `0.5`, `0` disables) with an inline comment documenting semantics and its
  interaction with `local_idle_admit_*` and `contention_queue_*`.
- Compute the gate before the economic `cached_ratio` computation so a rejected
  request costs nothing; keep `(skip, reason)` tuple shape for existing callers.
- Log the decision via the existing structured log line consumed by the
  observability item (do not add a new sink here; emit the fields).

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I need a bound on how many *distinct sessions* may hold a
local reservation for a large prompt at once ("N tenants, 2 slots"), so a new
session's large prompt cannot trash a resident session's KV to get a slot.

## Scope

Add the tenancy check to the local dispatch path
(`router_helpers._try_acquire_local_dispatch()` plus its release/cleanup siblings):
at most `server.local_session_tenants` (default = resolved slot count, i.e. 2)
distinct sessions may hold a large-prompt local reservation simultaneously. A new
session is admitted only when a slot is free of other sessions' prefixes, or when the
resident session's tenancy has idle-lapsed
(`server.local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds`). Beyond that bound the request follows
the normal chain rather than evicting a resident session.

**Resolved OPEN QUESTION (from the parent Appendix):** the tenancy idle-lapse default
derives from the **adaptive dispatch lease** (`local_dispatch_lease_*`, 30 s base →
1500 s cap), not from the snapshot lifetimes — one lifecycle, already tuned and
already bounded by the 180 s / 900 s watchdogs. The producer's recommended option is
adopted (no answer was supplied by the producer at planning time).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — Session tenancy ("N tenants, 2 slots").** At most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions (default: the slot count, i.e. 2) may hold a local reservation for a large prompt at once, and a new session's large prompt is admitted only when a slot is free of other sessions' prefixes or the resident session's tenancy has idle-lapsed.
- **AC2 — tenancy denial:** a unit test asserts that at most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions hold a large-prompt local reservation at once, that the (N+1)th distinct session's large prompt is denied with reason `tenant_limit` (following the normal fall-through chain, not evicting a resident), and that the denial does not consume the `contention_queue_*` budget differently from today's bypass path.
- **AC2 — same-session re-entry always permitted:** a test asserts a session's own second turn never waits behind its own earlier turn (existing lease semantics are preserved; tenancy only gates *new* sessions).
- **AC2 — idle-lapse releases tenancy:** a test asserts a resident session whose tenancy has exceeded `local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds` (derived from the adaptive dispatch lease) no longer blocks a new session, and that a *live* resident (data chunks / prefill progress / connected client) is never lapsed out.
- **AC2 — default is the slot count:** with `local_session_tenants` unset the bound is the resolved `session_slot_pool_size` (2); the value is configurable and non-positive/malformed values fall back to the slot count rather than disabling admission.
- **Idle-awareness + thrash-cooldown interaction unchanged:** regression tests assert `local_idle_admit_enabled` still admits on an idle GPU and that the post-deadline thrash cooldown (`LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL`) still applies to a tenancy-denied session.
- The AC2 unit tests from the test-harness item lose their `xfail` markers and pass through the test skill.

## Implementation sketch

- Register tenancy alongside the existing dispatch records (no new lifecycle
  machinery): a small in-memory map `session_id -> tenancy state` owned by the same
  lock that guards `local_active_queries` / `local_dispatch_records`, to preserve the
  documented lock ordering (`local_active_queries_lock` first).
- Lapse on idle using the existing adaptive lease timing source rather than a new
  timer; never extend on a merely open upstream socket.
- Add `local_session_tenants` and `local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds` to
  `proxy/config.yaml` `server:` with inline documentation.

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`

## Goal

As a client whose connection died, I must not leave a dead session holding the
local pool: tenancy reservations must behave as leases — reclaimed by the proxy
alone, within bounded windows — and the evicted session's KV snapshot must be saved
so a returning client restores warm instead of prefilling cold.

## Scope

Make the tenancy reservation follow the existing dispatch-record lease pattern and
wire its reclaim into the existing machinery: `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` (~10 s),
the 180 s no-progress watchdog, and the 900 s lifetime ceiling. On reclaim, save the
evicted session's KV snapshot (`slot_<id>.bin`, subject to the existing pool-size and
busy gates) and free the slot assignment. No new reaper task, no client protocol
change — the proxy is the sole owner of abandonment reaping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Tenancy reservations are leases, not locks.** Reservations follow the existing dispatch-record lease pattern: held only while real activity is observed (data chunks, prefill progress, or a live client), TTL refresh bounded by the 180 s no-progress watchdog and the 900 s lifetime ceiling, never extended by a merely open upstream socket, with reclaim via the existing ~10 s `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` and the evicted session's KV snapshot saved (`slot_<id>.bin`).
- **AC6 — reservations are leases, not locks:** a test asserts a reservation is held only while real activity is observed (data chunks, prefill progress, or a live client confirmed by the poll-cadence `request.is_disconnected()`), and that a merely open upstream socket never extends it.
- **AC6 — fast reclaim on observed disconnect:** a test asserts that when a disconnect is observed the reservation is released within one `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` cycle — record released, prefill marker popped, slot assignment freed, captured upstream `stream_cm` cancelled.
- **AC6 — bounded reclaim on a silent half-open drop:** a test asserts release within `<= 180 s` via the no-progress watchdog, and that no path lets a dead session gate the pool beyond those bounds (the 2026-10-23 ~5.5–6 min `local_lease_active` window is the regression baseline; the 900 s lifetime ceiling is never the only release path).
- **AC6 — snapshot saved on eviction:** a test asserts that on reclaim the evicted session's KV snapshot is saved as `slot_<id>.bin` subject to the pool-size and busy gates, so a returning client restores warm instead of prefilling cold.
- **AC6/AC5 — reuse the shared eviction event:** a test asserts the release path emits the **ERROR-level eviction event defined by `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` AC7** (post-acceptance eviction = ERROR, structured reasons such as `lease_evicted` / `slot_assignment_freed`) extended with this item's tenancy-specific reasons (resident prefix evicted by another tenant, tenancy lease expired) — no second logging convention is introduced. Cross-item dependency recorded on the parent item (comment 2026-10-25T01:01:22Z).

- The AC6 unit tests from the test-harness item lose their `xfail` markers and pass through the test skill.

## Implementation sketch

- Reuse `disconnect_reaper.py`'s observation signal rather than polling `/slots`;
  reuse the adaptive lease timing and the existing prefill marker bookkeeping.

- Call the existing `_save_slot_snapshot` / `_free_slot_assignment` helpers on

- Emit the eviction record through the shared event from `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`
  AC7 (extend its structured `reason` vocabulary) — never a parallel logger call.

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I want, per admission decision, the measured reusable prefix
and which session owned the slot — and as the capacity analyst, I want the usage
report to split resident-vs-evicted reuse and show slot-owner churn per session — so
residency regressions are visible without forensics.

## Scope

Emit the new fields on the existing structured log lines (no new sink) and extend the
usage report. Fields: `n_past_actual`, `estimated_tokens`, `reuse_ratio`,
`slot_owner_session`, and `decision` (`admit` / `resident_prefix_insufficient` /
`tenant_limit`) at `routing_skip_local` / `routing_hop` level. Extend
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` with a
resident-vs-evicted reuse section and per-session slot-owner churn.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Goal

Provide the regression oracle for the whole item **before** any behaviour changes: a checked-in fixture of the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 prefill-thrash window plus a replay harness that reproduces today's measured baseline. Later children (budget, pricing, eviction counter) assert their post-change behaviour against this harness, so the parent's AC4 has an executable baseline instead of a prose anecdote.

## Context

Baseline measured from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (`proxy.log*` + `llama-server.log*`) in the parent item: **160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events**, 45 local tasks cancelled mid-prefill, **~780k of ~840k prefill tokens computed then discarded (~93 %)**. Rotated, gzipped logs for that window are still on the host, so the fixture can be captured deterministically.

## Scope

**In:** capture command (documented), fixture file, replay harness, baseline assertions against today's code.

**Out:** any change to admission behaviour; any new config key; any production code change other than (optionally) a pure helper needed by the harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fixture captured and checked in.** A JSONL fixture records, for every local dispatch attempt in the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 window, at least: `ts`, `session`, `estimated_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `new_tokens`, admission verdict/reason as logged today, outcome (`prefill_deadline_exceeded` | `first_byte_ok` | `other`), and prefill tokens computed before cancellation. The fixture header documents the capture command (gzipped-log aware) so it can be regenerated.
- **AC2 — Replay harness reproduces the baseline.** Replaying the fixture through the current admission path (real `prefill_eta` estimator with a documented, fixture-pinned calibration profile) reproduces the measured baseline within tolerance: ≥150 deadline-cancelled attempts, ~45 cancelled tasks, ≥700k wasted prefill tokens. Assertion lives in `proxy/tests/`, runs green on today's `dev`.
- **AC3 — Replay results are exposed to tests, not eyeballs.** The harness returns a structured result object (per-attempt verdicts, aggregate counters: admitted, refused, deadline-cancelled, wasted tokens) so later children can assert on it without re-parsing logs.
- **AC4 — Vitest/pytest conventions respected.** Test file follows the repo's pytest style and the shared test-writing guidelines (behaviour assertions, no source greps, no placeholders); fixture size is bounded (< 2 MB) and contains no credentials, API keys, or full prompt bodies.
- **AC5 — Documented non-goal.** Harness is an analysis tool: it must not be imported by production modules (`proxy/proxy/*.py` imports of the harness = test failure).

- `proxy/tests/fixtures/prefill_thrash_2026_10_24.jsonl` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_window_replay.py` (new)

1. Write the capture command (shell one-liner in the fixture header + a `tools/` helper if it grows), join proxy admission lines with llama-server prefill progress lines per session/task.
2. Reduce to the minimal per-attempt records above; strip model text, keep only sizes/ratios/verdicts.

- None. Ships green on today's `dev`; it is the test-first item for this parent.

## Goal

Land the configuration surface that the behaviour children consume: the new cold-prefill budget keys, the widened prefill deadline, and a fail-fast assertion that keeps the timeout ordering coherent — with the documented units, interactions and rollback values the parent's AC6 demands.

## Context

Parent item's proposal table. The intake comment says "deadline 110" while the parent description (updated later) says **120**: 120 is authoritative (AC2/AC3 revenue maths: 25k at 249 t/s ≈ 100 s, p75 ≈ 93 s; 0.95 × 120 = 114 s). Today `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` and the p75 percentile-pricing floor is the hard-coded `CONSERVATIVE_MIN_TOKENS = 32_768` in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`.

## Scope

**In:** `proxy/config.yaml` keys + comments, `GuardConfig` fields with legacy-safe defaults, startup ordering validation, tests, doc updates.

**Out:** any change to the admission *decision* logic (child "Enforce cold-prefill budget on all admission paths" does that), any slot-count change, any change to `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold` derivation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Keys shipped (parent AC2/AC3/AC6 config half).** `proxy/config.yaml` server section carries `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`, `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`, `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`, `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`, `local_admission_guard_reference_tokens: 25000`, each with a comment stating units, meaning, and interaction with `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold` and the admission guard.
- **AC2 — Legacy-safe defaults.** `prefill_eta.resolve_config` exposes the three new values on `GuardConfig`; when a key is absent the resolved value reproduces today's behaviour exactly (budget `0` = disabled, percentile-min `32768`, safety fraction `0.0` = off), so every other config file/test that omits them is unchanged. Unit tests cover absent, present, and malformed values (malformed falls back to the default with a WARNING, matching the existing `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile` handling). A `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` above `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` produces a startup WARNING (percentile pricing would never engage, so the band guard would be silently dead).
- **AC3 — Deadline + ordering (parent AC2):** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`. Enforce and assert the ordering `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)`, and keep the deadline strictly below the client's 900 s queue deadline (config-load assertion). The assertion lives in startup validation: a violating config is FATAL (`ValueError` naming the offending values, in the same style as `_startup_validate_local_routing_config`). Tests assert (a) the shipped config passes, (b) each inversion — queue ≥ deadline, deadline ≥ first-byte ceiling, first-byte ceiling > max-prefill, deadline ≥ 900 — is rejected.
- **AC4 — Rollback documented (parent AC6).** Comments and `proxy/docs/routing.md` state the rollback set (budget `0`, deadline `90`, percentile-min `32768`, safety fraction `0.0`) and what each reverts.
- **AC5 — No behaviour change yet.** With the shipped config present but the decision logic unchanged, the existing suite stays green; the ordering validator is the only new refusal path.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/config_test.yaml`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_idle_admit_config_docs.py`

## Implementation sketch

1. Add constants + `GuardConfig` fields + parsing/validation in `prefill_eta.resolve_config` (reuse `_int_setting` / `_float_setting`).
2. Add `validate_prefill_timeout_ordering(config) -> list[str]` next to the resolver, returning FATAL-prefixed problems.
3. Call it from a new `_startup_validate_prefill_timeout_config` in `proxy/proxy/server.py` alongside the existing startup validators.
4. Update `config.yaml` comments and `docs/routing.md`; extend the docs test that guards config documentation.

data.description:
## Goal

Make the proxy refuse, at admission time, any local prefill whose **new (to-be-prefilled) tokens** cannot finish before the prefill deadline — on **every** admission path, including the idle/economic bypass — so a doomed prefill is never dispatched and then cancelled (parent AC1, AC3, AC5).

## Context

Today the guard refuses on projected **wait** (vs `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, 60 s) and on projected **first-byte ETA** (vs `local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, 90 s) only when the `(model, bucket)` window is calibrated, and the conservative p75 pricing only applies from the hard-coded `CONSERVATIVE_MIN_TOKENS = 32_768` upward. Result in the 2026-10-24 window: 160 deadline cancellations and ~93 % wasted prefill tokens. Two leaks matter:

- The **flat cap is missing**: nothing bounds `new_tokens`, so a 38k cold prompt is admitted whenever the point estimate happens to look affordable (and a 93k cold prompt whenever the bucket lacks samples, because the guard is then inert).
- The **idle/economic bypass** (`_evaluate_idle_admission_override` → `routing_idle_admit`, `local_idle_admit_enabled: true`) admits `large_context_bypass` requests **without consulting the ETA guard at all** — 38 oversized admissions in the measured window.

## Scope

**In:** `prefill_eta.evaluate_admission` (budget + deadline-relative pricing), `provider._evaluate_idle_admission_override` / `routing_idle_admit`, `admission_reserve` (reserve endpoint), guard logging (`reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`), tests.

**Out:** scheduler/tenancy work (LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG), slot-count changes, chain/fallback policy changes, any change to `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold` derivation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Budget (parent AC1):** `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000` caps the **new (prefilled) tokens** admitted for a local dispatch, on all admission paths (including idle/economic bypass). Over-budget requests are refused at admission (skip local, chain detours), never dispatched and never cancelled at the deadline. Concretely: refuse when `estimated_tokens * (1 - cached_ratio) > 25000` with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`; boundary tests are 24,999 and 25,000 admitted (inclusive) and 25,001 refused; the check is independent of calibration and of the caller's wait budget — it prices GPU compute, not queue patience, so it also binds for `high` priority where `wait_budget == 0` and for uncalibrated `(model, bucket)` windows.
- **AC2 — Refusal happens at admission, never dispatch-then-cancel (parent AC1).** The refusal is returned before the local POST: the request skips local and continues down the chain with a logged, parseable reason. Integration test asserts no local dispatch record and no `prefill_deadline_exceeded` follows a budget refusal.
- **AC3 — Every admission path is covered (parent AC1).** Unit + integration tests prove the budget binds on: (a) the contention-queue entry guard, (b) the direct free-slot guard, (c) the idle/economic bypass (`routing_idle_admit` — a `large_context_bypass` request over budget must NOT be admitted just because the GPU is idle), (d) `POST /llama/local/reserve`. One shared implementation only — no duplicated budget maths in any path.
- **AC4 — Deadline-relative pricing (parent AC3).** p75 percentile pricing applies from `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` (20000) upward instead of the hard-coded 32 768, and admission requires `eta_prefill <= local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction × local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (0.95 × 120 = 114 s). Tests: 25k in the 20–30k band (p75 ≈ 270 t/s → ~93 s) admitted; 25k in the 30–40k band (p75 ≈ 190 t/s → ~132 s) refused; safety-fraction maths yields exactly 114 s at a 120 s deadline; safety fraction `0.0` disables the term (rollback).
- **AC5 — Warm path unchanged (parent AC5):** warm requests remain admissible when total prompt size exceeds 25k (assert e.g. a 47k prompt with `cached_ratio` 0.99 / 549 new tokens stays local). The budget never binds on total prompt size, only on new tokens.
- **AC6 — Fixture replay proves the fix (parent AC4 baseline).** Replaying the child fixture harness with the new config admits **zero** cold prompts with `new_tokens > 25000`; every measured >25k attempt is refused with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`. The pre-change baseline assertions stay intact (the harness gains a post-change mode rather than being rewritten).
- **AC7 — Observability.** Budget refusals are logged through the existing `local_admission_guard` line (parsed by the usage report) with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded` and evidence fields (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `budget_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `deadline_s`); idle-bypass refusals are attributable (they must not be silently routed as if idle were blocked).
- **AC8 — `observe` policy respected.** With `local_admission_guard_policy: observe` the new bounds log `reject` verdicts but do not refuse, matching existing behaviour; the shipped config stays `reject`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_window_replay.py`

## Implementation sketch

1. Extend `GuardConfig` consumers: flat budget check first (cheap, calibration-free), then percentile pricing with the configured floor, then the safety-fraction deadline term; keep `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline` as the deadline reason and add `prefill_budget_exceeded` as dominant when the flat cap fires.
2. Hoist the budget check above the `wait_budget <= 0` and `not calibrated` early returns so it can never be skipped.
3. Route the idle/economic bypass verdict through the same `evaluate_admission` call (with the budget enforced even when the GPU is idle), logging `routing_idle_admit` only on an admitted verdict.
4. Extend `record_guard_decision` evidence fields; keep the existing field names stable for the usage-report parser.
5. Add the boundary/band/warm/bypass tests and the fixture-replay post-change assertions.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Prefill budget/deadline config knobs + ordering assertion" (needs the resolved config keys).
- Blocked by "Cold-prefill thrash-window regression fixture harness" (needs the replay oracle for AC6).

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I need the change shipped safely and AC4's verification
vehicle armed correctly at deploy time, so the 24 h regression check can actually run
and the full-suite gate proves nothing else broke.

## Scope

Staged rollout of the ladder behind the documented knobs, the dev-push full-suite
gate (AC9), and the AC4 deliverable: retitle `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` from the provable
lower bound (`run no earlier than 2026-10-26T00:51Z`) to the deploy-derived instant —
the later of this item's deploy and `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`'s deploy, plus 24 h — and
record the pinned measurement window, the baseline re-anchoring query and the
scheduling-attributed classifier in that item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC4 — Deadline/thrash regression (re-anchored), verified by a mandatory follow-up work item.** On a 24 h window measured after `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is deployed, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are >= 90 % below that window's own re-anchored baseline, with verification executed by the follow-up item `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` (this item arms it and never substitutes its own measurement).
- **AC4 (deliverable) — follow-up verification item armed:** `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` is retitled to `24 h AC4 verification of resident-prefix admission — run no earlier than <ISO-8601 UTC instant>`, where the instant is max(deploy of this item, deploy of `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`) + 24 h; its description records the pinned window (start/end UTC), the baseline re-anchoring query, the `proxy-usage-analysis` invocation and the scheduling-attributed classifier, and it stays linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and related to `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`. AC4 itself is satisfied only by that item's 24 h result, never by this session's measurements.
- **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes at the dev-push gate (no ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation; the gate and the test skill own execution).
- **AC4 — pending-deploy arithmetic is explicit:** if `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` has not deployed when this item ships, the retitle records the arithmetic with that term marked pending (and a comment on both items), and the follow-up item is re-armed with the concrete instant once that deploy is known — the follow-up must never run before *both* deploys + 24 h.
- **Staged rollout is observable:** the ladder ships with `local_idle_admit_*` still effective and `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` documented as `0`-disables, and the first report cycle after deploy is checked to confirm the resident-vs-evicted split and the admission-decision counts appear (evidence recorded as a work-item comment).
- **No out-of-scope regressions:** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, `local_max_concurrent_prefills` and the snapshot pool size are unchanged in the shipped diff (verified explicitly and recorded).
- **AC4 — Title format:** the follow-up item `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` is retitled to `24 h AC4 verification of resident-prefix admission — run no earlier than <ISO-8601 UTC instant>`, where the instant is max(this item's deploy, `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`'s deploy) + 24 h.
- **AC4 — Description records the pinned measurement window (start/end UTC), the baseline re-anchoring query for that window, the `proxy-usage-analysis` invocation and the scheduling-attributed classifier** (live `reuse_ratio` below `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, or `slot_owner_session` changed between admission and the deadline event).
- **AC4 — Linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and related to `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`**, assigned to the operator's triage queue.
- **AC4 — AC4 is not satisfied by the implementing agent's own measurements:** it is satisfied only when the follow-up item reports its 24 h result across a pinned window measured after both deploys.

## Implementation sketch

- Merge the ladder to `dev` (never `main`), let the pre-push hook run the full suite,
  then determine the deploy instant from the running proxy and the
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` deploy record.
- Retitle + re-describe the follow-up item with the concrete ISO-8601 instant; comment
  the derivation on both items so the arithmetic is auditable.
- Post one post-deploy comment with the first report cycle's admission-decision counts.

- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`

Depends on every implementation, test and docs item in this decomposition.

## Decomposition (parent `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`)

Sibling items created by the plan session (2026-10-25). Execute in dependency order;
test items precede implementation items.

| Step | Item id | Scope | Depends on |
|------|---------|-------|------------|
| C1 | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H | Test harness (this item) | — |
| C2 | LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 | Shared residency view | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H |
| C3 | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA | Resident-prefix gate + live pricing | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 |
| C4 | LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI | Session tenancy bound | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 |

data.description:
## Goal

Make post-acceptance eviction of a local dispatch an unambiguous **defect signal**: every release path that evicts an accepted dispatch *before its first byte* emits exactly one structured **ERROR** event with the full evidence set, and a dedicated monotonic counter tracks it (parent AC7, core half).

## Context

An accepted dispatch can be released before producing a first byte by six paths, and today each logs at a different level with no shared evidence:

| AC7 reason | Today's code path | Today's level |
|---|---|---|
| `prefill_deadline` | `router.py` `prefill_deadline_exceeded` + `router_helpers._release_prefill_deadline_dispatch` (`lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`) | WARNING / INFO |
| `no_progress_watchdog` | `router_helpers._cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` phase 1 (`reason=no_progress_watchdog`) | WARNING |
| `idle_timeout` | same function, inactive record past `expires_at` (`reason=idle_timeout`) | INFO |
| `orphan_cleanup` | same function, phase 3 (`reason=orphan_cleanup`) | WARNING + INFO |
| `lease_evicted` | `server._release_lease_on_session_eviction` → `lease_released reason=session_evicted` | INFO |
| `slot_assignment_freed` | `session._free_slot_assignment` (slot registry entry released) | no line of its own |

`lease_evicted` and `slot_assignment_freed` are AC7 vocabulary that does not exist yet; dispatch records today carry no `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `slot_id` or first-byte flag, so the required evidence cannot be emitted without enriching the record at creation.

## Scope

**In:** dispatch-record enrichment, one shared emitter, ERROR-level structured event on all six paths, in-process counter + per-reason breakdown, `/admin/metrics` and Prometheus exposure, tests.

**Out:** the report/parser work (separate child), any change to *when* these paths fire (levels and evidence only), any change to the admission decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Post-acceptance eviction is an ERROR (parent AC7):** any local dispatch that was **accepted** (admitted, dispatch record created) and then **evicted before producing a first byte** must be recorded at **ERROR** log level — never WARNING/INFO — with a structured, machine-parseable event carrying at least: `session`, `reason` (`prefill_deadline` | `no_progress_watchdog` | `idle_timeout` | `orphan_cleanup` | `lease_evicted` | `slot_assignment_freed`), `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `elapsed_s`, `slot_id`, and the llama task id where known. This covers every release path an accepted dispatch can suffer, so eviction after acceptance is unambiguously an error condition rather than expected churn; refusals **before** acceptance stay at their current level (a budget/ETA refusal is normal operation, not an error). One shared emitter produces the single line, e.g. `local_eviction_after_acceptance session=… reason=… estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=… eta_prefill_s=… elapsed_s=… slot_id=… llama_task_id=…`, emitted exactly once per eviction.
- **AC2 — Complete evidence.** The record is enriched at creation (in `router_helpers`, where the dispatch record is created) with `estimated_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s` (the guard decision that admitted it, when known), `slot_id` and `llama_task_id` where known, plus an explicit `first_byte_seen` flag set when the first chunk arrives. Fields that are genuinely unknown are emitted as `unknown`/`0`, never omitted, so the line stays machine-parseable.
- **AC3 — Only accepted-and-unserved dispatches are errors.** `first_byte_seen == True` records are **not** eviction errors (a lease that expires after a served response is normal churn and stays at its current level). Records without a first-byte flag that are evicted for `idle_timeout` must be classified by the flag, not inferred from the path.
- **AC4 — Per-path tests.** For **each** of the six reasons, a test drives the release path and asserts exactly one ERROR-level `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event with all evidence fields, and asserts that no such event is emitted at WARNING/INFO. Inverse test: a pre-acceptance refusal (budget / ETA / admission guard) emits **no** event and does not increment the counter.
- **AC5 — Monotonic counter + per-reason breakdown.** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` increments exactly once per eviction, with a per-reason breakdown, reset only on process restart; exposed as a Prometheus counter (labelled by reason) and in the `/admin/metrics` JSON payload alongside the existing `guardrail_metrics` style blocks.
- **AC6 — Backwards-compatible logs.** Existing `lease_released … reason=…` lines keep their current names and levels (the report and other consumers parse them); the new structured ERROR line is additive, so a pre-change log parser still works.
- **AC7 — Triage-ready.** The event carries enough to file a `test-failure` item without log archaeology (reason + tokens + ETA + elapsed + slot), and the shipped config's budget/pricing admits it: a within-budget prompt must never produce this event (fixture replay: counter is 0).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_no_progress_watchdog.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_reuse_gap_analysis.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_eviction_after_acceptance.py` (new)

## Implementation sketch

1. Create the emitter (e.g. `proxy/proxy/local_eviction.py`) with `record_eviction_after_acceptance(srv=None, *, session, reason, record, extra)` → logs the ERROR line and increments the counter; idempotent per record (guard against double emit on a path that runs twice).
2. Enrich the dispatch record at creation and set `first_byte_seen` where the first chunk is observed.
3. Call the emitter from each of the six release paths, passing the record it already has; leave the existing log lines untouched.
4. Add the counter to `metrics.py` (`llama_local_evictions_after_acceptance_total{reason}`) and to `handlers.admin_metrics` JSON.
5. Write per-path tests + the inverse (refusal) test.

## Dependencies

- None (independent of the config/budget children). Must land before the usage-report child, which parses this event.

data.description:
## Goal

Surface post-acceptance evictions in the `proxy-usage-analysis` report and its `--json` summary, and record the alerting threshold plus the triage rule that turns each such event into a defect work item (parent AC7 reporting half, AC7(b), AC7(c)).

## Context

`summary_to_json` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` already exposes `local_admission_reject`, `local_admission_admit`, `local_idle_admit` and `errors_by_type`. The new ERROR event from the eviction child is not parsed yet, so the counter cannot be seen in the 24 h regression window (parent AC4) and the operator has no alert.

## Scope

**In:** log parser patterns, aggregation counters, `summary_to_json` keys, text report section, docs (alert threshold, triage rule).

**Out:** the proxy-side emitter (separate child), any change to existing report keys, alerting infrastructure outside the docs/report (no new Prometheus rule file unless one already exists to extend).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Parse.** `log_parser.py` recognises the `local_eviction_after_acceptance` ERROR line (all evidence fields, tolerant of missing `llama_task_id`/`slot_id`) and classifies it as its own event kind, never as a fallback/reason inheritance for neighbouring lines.
- **AC2 — Aggregate + JSON summary (parent AC7(a)).** `aggregation`/`reporting.summary_to_json` expose top-level `local_evictions_after_acceptance` (total) **and** a per-reason breakdown (e.g. `local_evictions_after_acceptance_by_reason`), with every one of the six reasons addressable (`prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup`, `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`). Keys are additive: existing keys and their values are unchanged (regression test on a pre-change log fixture).
- **AC3 — Text report.** The human-readable report prints the counter and its per-reason breakdown, with the alert threshold (>0 for within-budget prompts) stated inline; `--quiet` still suppresses it.
- **AC4 — Alerting threshold documented (parent AC7(b)).** The skill's `SKILL.md`/report doc states the threshold: **any** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` for within-budget prompts is an alert, not a trend to watch.
- **AC5 — Triage rule documented (parent AC7(c)).** A documented rule (usage-analysis skill doc and the proxy runbook) that any such ERROR is treated as a defect and filed as a critical `test-failure`-class work item via the triage path, because it is exactly the signal that the budget/pricing model is wrong for a prompt band.
- **AC6 — Tests.** Parser test (full line, partial line, absence), aggregation test (per-reason counts), `summary_to_json` test (keys present, zero when absent), report-text test, and a pre-change-log regression test proving no existing key changed.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_llama_log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md`

## Implementation sketch

1. Add the regex + event kind + parser branch alongside the existing local-admission parsing.
2. Add `eviction_events` to the analysis result, with a `by_reason` counter.
3. Emit the two additive keys in `summary_to_json` and a report block next to the admission-guard block.
4. Document the threshold and triage rule where the other report thresholds live.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Post-acceptance eviction ERROR events and counter" (needs the event format).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the A/B benchmark harness to produce valid measurements
in the **40-80k-token** band, because that is the band that produces the
multi-minute local first-byte tail and the only band in which a micro-batch
change can still help.

## Why

`docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS) measured 8.9k / 17.9k
/ 26.8k prompts, found the ubatch 1024->2048 win confined to ~18k (memory
bandwidth bound above), and closed with: *"If this is revisited: measure at
40k-80k tokens"*. The parent item is that revisit, so the harness must be
trustworthy at that size first. Today `build_prompt()` targets ~4 chars/token
without reporting llama-server's real `prompt_tokens`, `--sizes` is free-form,
and a single 80k prefill can take minutes under GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The harness records llama-server's reported `prompt_tokens` per sample
  and fails loudly when the delivered size deviates from the requested size by
  more than 10 %, so a mis-sized prompt cannot silently invalidate a bin.
- AC2: An end-to-end run at `--sizes 40960,61440,81920 --reps 3` produces a
  JSON result with per-size p50/p90 and the 20k+ headline aggregate within a
  documented time budget and timeout.
- AC3: Offline unit tests cover prompt sizing/token accounting, percentile
  aggregation, size-deviation rejection and argument validation - no live
  server required.
- AC4: `docs/dev/` records the band methodology and validity guards: unique
  prompt text per repetition, `cache_prompt: false`, the TTS/GPU-contention
  noise rule, and minimum reps.
- AC5: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - the A/B harness
- `tests/test_ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - offline harness tests
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior experiment record to extend

## Implementation sketch (test-first)

1. Extend the offline tests for the new validations.
2. Report and validate actual `prompt_tokens`; fail fast on a mis-sized bin.
3. Add a documented default band (`40960,61440,81920`) and a per-size timeout
   policy.
4. Record the methodology in `docs/dev/`.

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) -
  a 40-80k prompt must fit the per-slot context.

## Out of scope

Changing llama-server flags, routing or admission policy.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want `--ubatch-size` and `--batch-size` re-measured in the
40-80k band against a pre-registered win threshold, so the values shipped in
`models.ini` are justified by measurement rather than inherited.

## Context

- Current `[Qwen3]` launch flags: `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2
  --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0
  --cache-type-v q8_0 --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`,
  plus `flash-attn`.
- Prior A/B (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS, `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md`): 1.04x
  at p90 over 20k+ batches, reverted. Its close-out rule is that a retry must
  be measured at 40-80k.
- Geometry interacts: per-slot context (`--ctx-size / --parallel`) bounds the
  largest prompt the harness can send, so this item starts only after the
  geometry experiment has recorded its decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch configuration, each changed value justified by measurement rather than guesswork, or reverted and recorded.
- AC1: A hypothesis and numeric decision gate are written on this item BEFORE
  the first measurement (for example: adopt when p90 prompt-eval tok/s improves
  by >= 1.3x in the 60-80k bins with decode regression <= 2 %).
- AC2: Candidate values (`--ubatch-size` 2048 and 4096; `--batch-size` 8192 vs
  16384) are measured one variable at a time on arm-identical workloads with
  >= 3 reps using the 40-80k band harness; raw JSON is archived under
  `benchmark-results/`.
- AC3: Each knob gets an explicit adopt/revert decision with measured numbers;
  an adopted value is written to `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with the measurement
  and rollback value in the comment, a rejected value is recorded as reverted
  to 1024 / 8192.
- AC4: VRAM and stability are checked per arm (clean llama-server start, no
  OOM, `rocm-smi` within budget); the restart that empties the 40 GiB prompt
  cache is recorded so proxy first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC5: Any test or script asserting the flags is updated in the same change and
  the full suite is green via the test skill.
- AC6: If no value wins, the item completes with a recorded NO-GO and the
  parent's tuning scope narrows to the proxy-knob/ETA-guard half.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard and the prefill
deadline re-checked against the post-change prefill rates and the interaction
documented, so a faster GPU cannot silently make the budget/deadline wrong.

## Context

- Live knobs - deployed by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, do **not** re-tune without new
  evidence: `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`,
  `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile: 75`,
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 600`.
- The guard calibrates itself from a rolling window of per-dispatch samples
  `(coded_tokens, new_tokens, dispatch_to_first_byte_ms)` keyed by
  `(model, context bucket)`, so it re-calibrates automatically. But the budget
  (25k) and deadline (120 s) were derived from the OLD band rates (249 t/s at
  20-30k, 114 t/s at 63k). If prefill becomes materially faster, both may be
  re-derivable - a decision for measurement, not guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the configuration (llama-server launch flags and the prefill-related proxy knobs) where measurement justifies each change, otherwise left unchanged and recorded.
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's configuration and documentation are updated together, and the local_prefill_deadline_seconds / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC1: Matched before/after windows compare guard behaviour: admit vs reject
  counts by reason (`prefill_budget_exceeded`, `eta_exceeds_budget`,
  `prefill_deadline_exceeded`), thrash-cooldown events and cancelled prefills.
- AC2: The measured band rates (10-20k, 20-30k, 30-40k, 40-60k, 60-80k) are
  re-derived from the post-change window and compared numerically with the
  rates the budget and deadline were derived from.
- AC3: A decision is recorded on whether 25 000 tokens / 120 s remain optimal;
  any change is justified by AC1/AC2 numbers, shipped in one change with its
  config comment, and carries a documented rollback.
- AC4: The `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` <-> ETA-guard <->
  contention-queue interaction (the ordering invariant
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds < local_prefill_deadline_seconds <
  local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`)
  is documented in one authoritative place (config comments plus a `docs/dev/`
  note) and the tests asserting the ordering still pass.
- AC5: Guard/calibration code is unchanged unless a measured defect is found;
  if changed, unit tests cover the new behaviour.
- AC6: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` - calibration and admission guard
- `proxy/config.yaml` - guard, budget and deadline configuration
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta.py` - calibration tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` - conservative pricing tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` - deadline interaction tests
- `docs/dev/prefill-eta-deadline-interaction.md` - authoritative interaction note

## Dependencies

- Baseline prefill measurement capture.
- Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (the rates it changes).
- Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints.

## Out of scope

Re-litigating the values shipped by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D without new
post-change evidence.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the >60 % local-busy precondition measured and recorded on
the parent (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) **before** any geometry change, so the 1-vs-2
slot comparison is run against a contended GPU window instead of idle noise.

## Context

The parent's GATING PRECONDITION: local is currently ~10 % busy, so a 1-vs-2 slot
comparison would measure noise. The trade-off (overlapping sessions serialising
behind one slot) only appears when demand actually contends for slots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `proxy-usage-analysis` report is generated for a complete night window and its `## Local model utilization` section shows busy >= 60 % for that full window.
- AC2: The evidence (report path, window start/end, busy %, turns served, session count) is recorded as a comment on LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN before any configuration change.
- AC3: If busy < 60 %, the parent is left blocked with the measured number recorded: no arm is run and no geometry flag is changed.
- AC4: The exact window (start, end, length in hours) is recorded so Arm A and Arm B can be given identical-length windows.

- Parent AC0 trace: A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a repeatable measurement protocol plus an arm-comparison
reporter, so both geometry arms are measured over identical windows with
identical metrics and tooling (parent AC1, AC3).

## Context

- Precedent: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` (A/B harness that archives raw JSON under `benchmark-results/` and pre-registers a numeric gate).
- Metrics come from two sources: the proxy-usage-analysis report (`local_busy` prefill/decode split, turns served, fallback reasons) and `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (dispatch -> first byte, queue waits, errors).
- Per-slot context is derived, never configured directly: `--ctx-size / --parallel`, clamped by `effective_per_slot_threshold()` (`ctx_size // slots - 4096`), i.e. 2 slots -> 126,976 and 1 slot -> 258,048.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` records the arm definitions (A = 2 x 131,072 current; B = 1 x 262,144), the identical window length and the preferred same-weekday night span, the per-arm metric list, the exact commands, the raw-data archive naming convention, and the **pre-registered numeric decision gate written before any measurement**; a protocol summary (window length, metric list, decision gate) is also recorded on the parent LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN (parent AC1: 'defined and written on this item').
- AC2: `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` emits, per arm, every metric the parent's AC3 names: local busy %, turns served locally, diverts per fallback reason (notably `context_too_large` and `large_context_bypass`), queue wait / `fallback_after_queue` counts, time to first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and error counts (`slot_save failed`, HTTP 400/503).
- AC3: The reporter is covered by fixture-driven tests: one green path per metric plus missing-log and malformed-line paths, so a metric that silently reads zero fails the suite.
- AC4: An arm apply/verify helper (`scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` or an equivalent documented procedure) applies an arm's geometry (parallel, per-slot ctx, `session_slot_pool_size`, warm/cold thresholds) and verifies post-restart reality from llama-server (n_ctx per slot and slot count), refusing to report success on mismatch.
- AC5: The protocol records the restart/cache-loss marker procedure, so first-byte statistics are never compared across a restart that emptied the 40 GiB prompt cache.

- Parent AC1 trace: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item, and summarised on the parent item as well.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` - new arm-comparison reporter
- `tests/test_slot_geometry_ab_report.py` - fixture-driven reporter tests
- `scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` - arm apply/verify helper
- `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` - protocol and pre-registered decision gate

- Can start before the busy gate is met (desk work, no GPU reconfiguration).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want Arm A (the current 2 x 131,072 geometry) captured over a
gate-compliant night window, so there is a like-for-like baseline for Arm B.

## Context

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC3: The reporter output for Arm A (every protocol metric) is recorded on this item and on the parent.

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want Arm B (1 slot at 262,144 ctx) measured over a window of
identical length to Arm A, with the slot-count and context-dependent settings
adjusted consistently, so the geometry trade-off is measurable without a
threshold confound.

## Context

- Per-slot ctx is `--ctx-size / --parallel`: `--parallel 1 --ctx-size 262144` -> 262,144 per slot. `--parallel` and `session_slot_pool_size` MUST match or sessions map to nonexistent slots.
- The warm ceiling is `min(clamp, economic)` with economic = `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio x local_model_ctx_size)` (0.4578 x 262,144 ~= 120,049) and clamp = 258,048 at 1 slot. Leaving the ratio unchanged keeps the warm cap at ~120K, so the extra slot context would never be routed to - the ratio/threshold must be raised so the ceiling matches the new clamp (parent AC2: "adjusted consistently").
- The cold/warm band must keep non-zero width or the cached_ratio routing check stays unreachable (LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` becomes moot with one slot (prefill serialisation is inherent); record whether it is left as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Geometry changes are applied together and verified after restart: llama-server reports 1 slot with n_ctx 262,144, `session_slot_pool_size: 1`, warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp (or an explicit recorded justification for keeping ~120K), cold threshold unchanged at 38,000. Band width and cached_ratio-check reachability are demonstrated from the routing code / unit tests, not assumed.
- AC2: Arm B is measured over a window of the same length as Arm A inside a >= 60 % busy night; raw data archived under `benchmark-results/`; reporter output recorded on this item and on the parent.
- AC3: A rollback is recorded (exact values and command to restore Arm A) and the cache-emptying restart is marked so first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC4: Any serving errors introduced (slot_save failed, HTTP 400/503, slot-mismatch warnings) are captured in the arm's metric table.

- Parent AC2 trace: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a comparable period at the gate, with llama-server --parallel / --ctx-size changed together and session_slot_pool_size plus the warm/cold thresholds adjusted consistently.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/config.yaml` - `session_slot_pool_size`, `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio`, `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`, `local_model_ctx_size`

## Problem statement

Found while verifying the live rollout of `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` AC5
(2026-10-25, dev tip `10ac97c6`, proxy pid 2830344).

`provider._log_residency_decision()` emits `reuse_ratio` straight from
`ResidentPrefixFacts.reuse_ratio`. For a session with **no slot of its own**
(`residency_source=non_resident`) and for genuinely unknown state
(`residency_source=unknown`), `resolve_resident_prefix()` returns
`reuse_ratio=0.0` as an internal *sentinel* (the gate needs a number to compare
against `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`), and that sentinel is logged as if it
were a measurement:

```
routing_resident_prefix ... decision=resident_prefix_insufficient n_past_actual=none estimated_tokens=78968 reuse_ratio=0.0000 slot_owner_session=... residency_source=non_resident ...
```

`proxy-usage-analysis` then classifies those decisions as *measured*
(`reuse_ratio is not None`), so the new `## Residency-aware admission` section
reported "Residency decisions: 3 (measured ratio: 3)" and "Evicted (denied): 3
with a measured prefix" for a window where **nothing was measured at all**
(`n_past_actual=none` on every line). Observed live:

```
- Residency decisions: 3 (measured ratio: 3, no measurement: 0)
- Evicted denials (resident_prefix_insufficient): 3 with a measured prefix, 0 with no slot at all
| Evicted (denied) | 3 | median 0.0%, p10 0.0%, max 0.0% | 78968 | - |
```

That inverts the section's purpose: the resident-vs-evicted reuse split exists
to distinguish *measured* reuse from *no measurement*, and the noise direction
matters - a fabricated 0 % drags the evicted median down and hides the
`context_tokens`-unreported population the fallback ladder is about.

## Expected behaviour

A decision with **no measurement** (`n_past_actual is None`: non-resident, or
unknown state) logs `reuse_ratio=none`, matching `n_past_actual=none`. A real
measurement of zero (a slot that reported `context_tokens=0`) still logs
`reuse_ratio=0.0000` - the two must stay distinguishable. Internal gate
arithmetic is unchanged (the sentinel stays internal).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_log_residency_decision()`; the `reuse_ratio=` field is emitted here and must report `none` when `n_past_actual=none` (the 0.0 sentinel in `ResidentPrefixFacts` stays internal to the gate).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — `RE_REUSE_RATIO` / `parse_log_line()`; already maps `reuse_ratio=none` to `None`, so the measured/non-measured split is a parser-level contract.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — `_append_residency_section()`; `measured`/`no_slot` partition and the resident/evicted ratio rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` — AC1/AC3 log-shape tests parsed through the real `proxy-usage-analysis` parser.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — AC2 report-split test (`TestResidencyAdmission`).

## Scope decision (plan)

Single vertical slice: one log field in `provider.py`, its parser/report consumers
(already tolerant of `none`), and the two regression tests. No feature
decomposition and no phasing are warranted — the item is one atomic contract
change (log sentinel separation) touching three files plus tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 - no fabricated measurement in the log:** `routing_resident_prefix`
  emits `reuse_ratio=none` whenever `n_past_actual=none` (sources
  `non_resident` and `unknown`), and still emits the numeric ratio when a slot
  reported `context_tokens` (including a genuine 0).
- **AC2 - the report splits the two populations:** with non-measurement lines,
  `proxy-usage-analysis` reports those decisions under "no measurement" /
  "with no slot at all" and **not** in the "measured ratio" denominator or the
  resident/evicted ratio rows.
- **AC3 - regression tests:** a unit test asserts both shapes (`none` for
  non-resident/unknown, numeric for measured, including 0) end to end through
  the real parser; a test asserts the gate decision itself is unchanged (still
  `resident_prefix_insufficient`).
- **AC4 - full project test suite passes** at the dev-push gate.
data.title: routing_resident_prefix logs reuse_ratio=0.0000 for non-resident sessions, so the usage report counts a non-measurement as a measured prefix

# Pin start-proxy.sh shell-level `--restart` preserve-vs-restart decision with a pytest test

## Problem statement

`start-proxy.sh --restart` decides whether to preserve a warm llama-server by
comparing the `config_sha256` recorded in `.llama_server_signature.json` with a
freshly computed `merged_config_sha256` of `proxy/config.yaml`; on a match it
preserves ("Preserving running llama-server (unchanged local backend config)."),
otherwise it kills and restarts llama-server. That shell branch is currently
the **only** untested consumer of the merged-config signature: the sole
coverage lives in `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, which
LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 deletes (mode-era harness). The Python tests cover the hash
helper and the signature writer (`proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`,
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`), not the shell decision that acts on
them — so a regression there (e.g. comparing the wrong path, ignoring the flag)
would go unnoticed and would either kill a warm llama-server on every restart
or silently preserve a stale one.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — the warm KV/prompt cache must survive a proxy-only
  restart, and a genuine local-backend change must restart llama-server.
- **Future implementation agents** — need the shell branch pinned so changes to
  `start-proxy.sh` restart handling fail loudly in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Unchanged config preserves llama-server.** A pytest test runs a
  sandboxed copy of `start-proxy.sh --foreground --restart` whose signature
  file matches `merged_config_sha256(proxy/config.yaml, proxy/config.yaml)` and
  asserts the "Preserving running llama-server" line is emitted and the fake
  `pkill` log contains **no** `llama-server` kill.
- **AC2 — Changed config restarts llama-server.** With the sandbox config
  edited after the signature was written (merged hash changes), the preserving
  line is absent and the fake `pkill` log shows a `llama-server` kill.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe signatures.** Missing, empty or corrupt signature /
  unreadable hash → conservative restart (never an unearned preserve), asserted
  behaviourally.
- **AC4 — Explicit override still wins.** `--keep-llama-server` forces
  preservation even when the signature mismatches (flag beats hash).
- **AC5 — Sandbox isolation.** The test copies the script into a temp dir with
  stubbed `pkill`/`fuser`/`ss`/`netstat`, an isolated `$HOME`, an ephemeral port
  and a fake interpreter intercepting the final `exec uvicorn`; it never
  touches the live proxy, llama-server, TTS or ports 8000/8080/8081, and never
  issues a blanket kill. It is collected by the default pytest suite (unlike
  the bare `tests/*.sh` harnesses).
- **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.**
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to `start-proxy.sh`: this is coverage for the existing
  contract. A defect found while writing it becomes a separate work item.
- Reuse the established sandbox pattern in
  `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` (fake `python3` recording argv,
  stubbed process/port probes) rather than inventing a new harness.
- The signature schema is written by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
  (`_write_llama_server_signature`: `mode`, `model`, `parallel`, `router_mode`,
  `config_sha256`); fixtures must match it.
- UK English.

## Existing state

- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (being deleted by LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29) holds
  the only behavioural assertions for this branch; after deletion the branch has
  none.
- `grep -rln "Preserving running llama-server"` matches only that harness and
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` asserts the flag is *documented*
  (`test_start_proxy_help_documents_keep_llama_server`) and pins the Python hash
  helper — not the shell preserve/restart decision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_signature.py` — new pytest test (name
  indicative).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` — sandbox pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — script under test (read-only).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `merged_config_sha256` fixture hash.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — signature schema reference.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — deletes the stale mode-era harness; this item
  replaces the one piece of live coverage that deletion removes.
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H**, **LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8** — duplicate items closed
  in favour of LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 (producer decision B).
- **LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW** — restart signature hashes the merged config.
- **LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN** — preserve-the-warm-llama-server design.
